articles.title: Colombia peace deal must endure as insecurity grows, Security Council hears

paras.en: Colombia peace deal must endure as insecurity grows, Security Council hears

Nearly 10 years after Colombia signed a historic peace agreement to end a decades-long insurgency, the deal is under strain from growing insecurity – and the UN’s top official in the country says it cannot be allowed to falter.

Miroslav Jenča told the Security Council on Monday that the 2016 accord must be implemented in full, with proper funding, better coordination between institutions and protection for former combatants.

He pointed to real gains: rural development, and mechanisms for transitional justice and reparation for victims. But he admitted that implementation has had “many shortcomings” and that much remains to be done.
Security policy and the peace agreement should reinforce each other, Mr. Jenča said, and the accord should be carried out comprehensively.

“We look forward to the further definition of its policies, and we stand ready to support the Government in this regard,” he said, offering the experience gained by the UN Verification Mission over almost a decade of supporting implementation.

Communities in conflict-affected regions remain exposed to armed groups, geographical isolation and limited access to public services. Child recruitment, particularly among ethnic communities, and threats and attacks against women remain major concerns, ambassadors heard.
Government data presented to legislators show that illegal armed groups grew from around 15,000 members in 2022 to approximately 28,000 today.
Mr. Jenča also condemned the killings of civil society leaders María Ovidia Palechor and James Flor in Cauca on 1 September, highlighting the risks faced by rights defenders.
He said expanding economic opportunities, improving public services and strengthening local institutions were essential to reducing violence.
Despite these challenges, more than 11,000 former members of the FARC-EP rebel group remain committed to reintegration.
With State and international support, they have developed around 6,000 productive projects and 300 cooperatives in sectors including agriculture, tourism, trade and textiles.
Mr. Jenča highlighted tourism initiatives involving former combatants and victims, aimed at stimulating local economies and job markets.
However, economic sustainability and security remain significant challenges. Since the agreement was signed in 2016, 501 former combatants have been killed, most recently on 22 September in Cesar.

The Special Representative reaffirmed the UN mission's readiness to continue supporting implementation and highlighted its value on the ground, noting that over almost a decade it had built relationships of trust in some of regions most impacted by continuing violence.
Colombia had entered “a new political chapter, with wide ranging challenges ahead,” Mr. Jenča said, calling for “sustained international engagement in order to overcome remaining obstacles.”

articles.title: General Assembly adopts pandemic declaration, but not by consensus

paras.en: General Assembly adopts pandemic declaration, but not by consensus

The General Assembly on Monday adopted a political declaration on pandemic prevention, preparedness and response, by 153 in favour to three against (Argentina, Israel and United States) with two abstentions (New Zealand and Paraguay).
The text was due to be approved by consensus at a high-level meeting on 25 September.
Objections from the United States and a few other States blocked that, pushing the issue back to the assembly.
Read the full political declaration here.
Chile’s representative summed up one prevailing view, saying that “no country, no matter how big it might be or how prepared it might be, can alone address a threat that knows no borders.”

The declaration is political and non-binding. It calls for stronger national, regional and international cooperation, guided by science, equity and respect for human rights, and it welcomes last year’s landmark adoption of the World Health Organization (WHO) Pandemic Agreement.

“WHO welcomes this strong commitment by UN Member States to continue working together on pandemic prevention, preparedness and response,” said World Health Organization chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus.

“The world has come a long way since COVID-19. We urge countries to now fulfil the commitments they have made – especially to finalize negotiations on the Pathogen Access and Benefit Sharing system (PABS) annex, so the WHO Pandemic Agreement can be opened for signature, begin the process of ratification and enter into force as international law.”
The agreement cannot be opened for signature until Member States complete the annex on pathogen access and benefit-sharing – the system by which countries would share samples and genetic data.
Those that do so would receive a share of any resulting vaccines, treatments and diagnostics.
Talks have stalled amid a standoff between developing countries and some high-income European nations together with the US.
The World Health Assembly – comprising the WHO’s 194 members – is due to return to the annex next May.
The US representative had previously cited “divisive ideologies that lack definitional consensus” as well as the declaration’s references to the continuing annex negotiations.

In addition to adopting the pandemic declaration, the 193-member world body had a number of items on its agenda on Monday, including the consideration of draft resolutions on the UN Declaration on Sea Level Rise and a political declaration of the high-level meeting to mark the 25th anniversary of the adoption of the anti-racism Durban Declaration and Programme of Action.
WHO aims to spot new outbreaks within 24 hours
The World Health Organization (WHO) on Monday launched a five-year strategy for its Hub for Pandemic and Epidemic Intelligence, with the goal of detecting emerging health threats within 24 hours.

Set up in 2021 during the COVID-19 pandemic, the hub wants every country to be able to identify and understand new threats quickly, so outbreaks can be contained before they become epidemics or spread internationally.

articles.title: London Lions given lesson by Portland in historic game for British basketball

paras.en: NBA: London Lions make history against Portland Trail Blazers but get a lesson in Oregon

Watch the 2026-27 NBA season, live on Sky Sports – starting with the Detroit Pistons hosting the Boston Celtics on Sky Sports Mix from 8pm on Tuesday 20 October, followed by LeBron James' competitive debut for the Philadelphia 76ers against the New York Knicks
The London Lions became the first British club to face an NBA team but suffered a heavy 119-66 defeat to the Portland Trail Blazers in Oregon on Monday.
London never led as Portland dominated throughout, leading for 99 per cent of the contest and stretching their advantage to as many as 57 points at one stage.
The Trail Blazers extended their lead in every quarter, going into the breaks 34-21, 72-33 and 100-49 ahead, having entered the game as 36.5-point favourites.
Portland shot 56 per cent from the field and made 16 of their 34 three-point attempts, while London managed just 30 per cent overall and went 7 of 33 from beyond the arc.
The hosts dominated inside, outscoring the Lions 54-24 in the paint and winning the rebounding battle 51-32.
Overall, Portland registered 32 assists on 45 made field goals and showcased some nice ball movement at the Moda Center as they moved to 2-0 in preseason action.
London also committed 24 turnovers, from which Portland scored 39 points, compared with just 14 points the Lions generated from their opponents' mistakes.
The game was played under NBA rules rather than European regulations, with 12-minute quarters instead of 10, a larger court and a three-point line further from the basket.
London briefly threatened to make a contest of it towards the end of the first quarter.

Ethan Price hit two three-pointers from 26 feet in the space of 40 seconds, both assisted by Devante Adams either side of a Deni Avdija layup, to bring the Lions within four points at 23-19 with three minutes remaining in the period.
But Portland took control with a 38-12 second quarter, including a 15-0 run over the final four minutes of the half.
Maxwell Lewis, the only London player with previous NBA experience, led the Lions with 13 points, five rebounds and a game-high four steals.

Adams added 12 points off the bench, while Price and Joel Scott contributed eight apiece. Six of Scott's points came in the fourth quarter, while Thomas Kennedy collected six rebounds, including three offensive boards.

Great Britain international Tarik Phillip endured a difficult night, missing all eight of his field-goal attempts, including five from three-point range. His three points came entirely from the free-throw line.
Portland's five starters played a combined 76 minutes for 45 points. None of them appeared after half-time.
Toumani Camara and Scoot Henderson led the Trail Blazers with 14 points each. Henderson made four of his five three-point attempts in just 16 minutes off the bench.

Yang Hansen added 13 points and four assists, including a three-pointer from 25 feet, while Sidy Cissoko also scored 13, shooting a perfect 5 of 5 from the field and making all three of his attempts from beyond the arc.
Jeremy Sochan, who grew up in England, finished with eight points and a game-high eight rebounds, while marquee name Ja Morant scored five points and dished five dimes.
Deni Avdija recorded a game-best plus-minus of +44 in 17 minutes, while London's Keenan Evans finished at -45 in 20 minutes.
Damian Lillard, Robert Williams III, Shaedon Sharpe and Chris Youngblood did not feature for the Trail Blazers.
Coach Sabonis returns to where his father made his name
London are coached by Tautvydas Sabonis, whose father Arvydas spent seven seasons with Portland across the 1990s and early 2000s. Tautvydas had not visited the city for more than a decade.
Sabonis admitted the timing of the trip was far from ideal.
"If I had to choose a different timing, I would definitely choose it in the preseason, not now," he said.
Last season was his first in charge of the Lions, who won all four domestic competitions.

London are the reigning Super League Basketball champions, have started this season 5-0 in the SLB and have won one of their opening two EuroCup group games. In 2024, they became the first British men's club to reach the EuroCup semi-finals.

The Lions made a round trip of almost 10,000 miles in the middle of their domestic and European campaigns, arriving in Portland on Saturday afternoon before departing immediately after the game. They host Skyliners Frankfurt in the EuroCup on Thursday.
To minimise jet lag, the squad remained on British time throughout their stay in Oregon, waking at around 4am for breakfast.
A historic meeting with implications beyond Portland

The closest British and NBA club basketball had previously come to such a meeting was the 1995 McDonald's Championship, when Sheffield Sharks and Houston Rockets participated in the same tournament but did not face each other.
The Lions have submitted a bid to join the EuroLeague, which has ambitions to expand from 20 to 24 clubs by the 2027-28 season.
Owned by Lithuanian technology company Tesonet, London also became the first British basketball club to wear Jordan Brand kit this season.
Meanwhile, the proposed NBA Europe competition has placed renewed attention on the British market, with London and Manchester both discussed as potential franchise cities.
Monday's exhibition was not connected to that project, but it offered the Lions an opportunity to test themselves against NBA opposition and put British club basketball on an international stage.
The result demonstrated the gulf between the teams. The occasion, however, was about more than the scoreline.

articles.title: Jaissle sorry for Coventry loss as Carra says Newcastle 'beaten up' again

paras.en: Matthias Jaissle: Newcastle boss apologises for Coventry loss as Jamie Carragher says they were 'beaten up'

Newcastle suffer second consecutive 4-1 away loss after defeat at Coventry; Toon boss Matthias Jaissle: "We can only apologise to the fans who came here"; Sky Sports' Jamie Carragher: "In their last two away games, they've been beaten up twice - and that's got to stop very quickly"
Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle has apologised to the travelling fans following their 4-1 loss at Coventry, as Jamie Carragher said they were "beaten up" once again on the road.
The Magpies' previous away game a month ago also saw them defeated 4-1 on the Monday Night Football at Leeds.
A second loss in three games comes after Jaissle had enjoyed an unbeaten five-game start across all competitions, but recent results have seen his side fall to 11th in the Premier League table.
A wasteful Newcastle lost at Coventry despite having 19 shots, three big chances and more than double the number of touches in the opposition box than the home side.
- Coventry 4-1 Newcastle - Match report & highlights
- Newcastle news & transfers⚫⚪ | Newcastle fixtures & scores | FREE Newcastle highlights▶️
- Got Sky? Watch Premier League games LIVE on your phone📱
- Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream PL games with no contract📺
Jaissle told Sky Sports: "We're frustrated. It's a feeling you don't want to have on a Monday evening after a match where you should win.
"We can only apologise to the fans who came here; they deserve a different result.
"We need to analyse it, clearly. There were bits that were good but, in both boxes, to defend our own goal we need to improve and also score goals.
"The opportunities were there, but the desire and hunger to finish the attacks was missing."
He added: "We need to improve on the things we can control, and that's a lot right now."
Newcastle have now conceded the joint-most goals in the league so far alongside Bournemouth and Chelsea.
The German said at his post-match press conference: "I think it was a tough story throughout the whole match. There were elements in both boxes where we need to step up and improve.
"It's not something we can compare with the Leeds match today because I think we were at least better.
"The goals we conceded, it was a different story. We were better after the first 10 minutes; we dominated the game but conceded easy goals, which we need to improve.
"If you conceded eight goals in two away matches on Monday evenings, then it's not good enough for the Premier League."
It is the first time since December 2012 that Newcastle have conceded four or more goals in back-to-back Premier League away games.
For Carragher, the heavy losses at Leeds and Coventry have raised questions over Newcastle's "lack of physicality".
Speaking on Monday Night Football, Sky Sports' Carragher said: "We've consistently said this season they've had a good start results-wise, but the underlying numbers haven't been great.
"How many shots they concede, their xG. You look at two away games now where they've lost 8-2.
"He's going with two strikers up there; I know (Yoane) Wissa drops a little bit deeper, but when Eddie Howe was there it was more of a 4-3-3.
"Every manager has their own way, but when you think of the lack of physicality in that team, it might be a case where you leave one of the strikers out and go with an extra body in midfield.
"It's a young team, and it isn't as physically powerful as a lot of the teams in the Premier League.
"And in their last two away games, they've been beaten up twice - and that's got to stop very quickly."
Analysis: Coventry teach Newcastle a lesson in finishing
On a night where they faced the Premier League's second-highest xG overperformers, it was Coventry who taught Newcastle a lesson in finishing at the CBS Arena.
It was one they had learned the hard way too, with the worst shot conversion of any team in the league coming into Monday's game and just one of 51 shots finding the back of the net to date.
But football is a funny old game. A 4-1 scoreline suggests Newcastle were outplayed, which could not be further from the truth, though they were certainly outfought.

Where Coventry stood resilient - even clearing off their own line from Matias Fernandez-Pardo once he had rounded Carl Rushworth - Newcastle caused too many of their own problems, and, for once, the Sky Blues took full advantage.

Three superb finishes, and an early penalty, saw them to their first Premier League home win in more than 9,000 days, but their finishing was still not Coventry's most impressive quality on the night.

That fortitude, digging in after taking an early lead and hanging on after Sven Botman's wonder strike had given Newcastle a glimmer of hope at 2-1, was what won them the day and, on fight at least, that was enough to crown them worthy winners.

They have already needed that mental strength to bounce back from four goalless and pointless games to start their Premier League return, and, in a league as punishing as this, that could be what decides whether they will stay there come May.

articles.title: State Department IG probing Kimberly Guilfoyle amid alleged $100,000 demand
articles.author: Garrett Haake

paras.en: U.S. Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle and the embassy she leads are under investigation by the State Department’s Office of the Inspector General, two people familiar with the decision confirmed to NBC News.

The government watchdog’s probe comes as legal consultant and longtime Donald Trump supporter and donor Eric Deters has accused Guilfoyle of asking him to pay her outstanding $100,000 American Express bill in the days before her 2025 confirmation hearing in exchange for access to senior administration officials.
“She was so desperate for that $100,000. It was a quid pro quo,” Deters told NBC News in an interview Thursday.

“She said I could ask her for anything and everything in Trump world. There was no request too big,” he said of Guilfoyle, a former Fox News personality, Trump campaign surrogate and ex-fiancee of Donald Trump Jr.

Deters provided NBC News with a PDF document of texts and Signal messages with Guilfoyle, which were first reported Wednesday by The Wall Street Journal. The Daily Mail first reported the watchdog investigation.

One of the messages provided by Deters appears to show Guilfoyle instructing him to wire the money directly to American Express because “it won’t show up anywhere” that way. He said he did not pay her the money.
An attorney for Guilfoyle did not respond to a request for comment, but told the Journal she disputed the authenticity of the messages while not providing specifics.
Vice President JD Vance said Friday that “these are accusations” and “we don’t try people in the court of public opinion.”
Deters’ claims, he said, are “one person’s story.”
“Let’s actually see what the facts are. Let’s see what the truth is, and obviously if there was something bad that happened, then people have to suffer consequences for it,” he said.

Rep. Gregory Meeks, the top Democrat on the House Foreign Affairs Committee, wrote to Secretary of State Marco Rubio last week asking for more information about additional allegations that appeared in The Wall Street Journal.
On Thursday, Rubio chided a reporter for asking him about the accusations against Guilfoyle while he was with her in Athens.

“We don’t conduct these things in a press conference on a tarmac in a foreign country because you wrote a story or somebody else wrote a story because some source gave it to you,” he said, adding: “I don’t even know if what you’re reporting is true.”

A senior diplomatic official, meanwhile, said the news of probe set off alarm bells throughout the State Department. The official described the investigation as rare and said that watchdog is known primarily for performing routine embassy inspections rather than investigations.
A spokesperson for the State Department inspector general’s office said the watchdog does not confirm, deny or comment on investigations.
The State Department declined to comment on the accusations against Guilfoyle or any investigation.
Watchdog investigations into potential ethics violations by U.S. ambassadors are rare, but not unprecedented.

During the first Trump administration, Woody Johnson, then the U.S. ambassador to the U.K. and a longtime Republican donor, was investigated by the State Department’s inspector general, who found he made “inappropriate” comments on race, gender and religion to embassy staff.

The State Department rejected recommendations for Johnson, saying he had watched a government video on workplace harassment and instructed senior officials to do the same, and also encouraged staff to take a training course on “mitigating unconscious bias.”

Under President Joe Biden in 2024, the watchdog investigated U.S. Ambassador to Singapore Jonathan Kaplan, finding the political appointee threatened his staff and failed to submit about $48,000 in travel expenses on time or with proper documentation.
In Kaplan’s case, State said it was taking the recommendations seriously and made organizational changes.

“The president always wants his representatives ... to manage people with dignity and respect,” former White House National Security Council spokesman John Kirby said at the time. “He’s comfortable that the State Department is taking this seriously.”

articles.title: Pope Leo to be hospitalized Tuesday for surgery to remove a lung nodule
articles.author: The Associated Press

paras.en: Pope Leo XIV will be admitted to a hospital Tuesday morning to undergo surgery to remove a lung nodule discovered during recent medical tests, the Vatican said Monday.
The timing of the procedure was confirmed after the 71-year-old American pontiff had a full day of meetings, audiences and appointments.
The Vatican press office also said no particular issue precipitated the tests, denying Italian media reports suggesting an inflammation had prompted the medical checkup.
Leo revealed the discovery during his Sunday noon prayer and said he was following doctors’ advice to remove the nodule “in the coming days.” The Vatican predicted a weeklong recovery.

It was business as usual at the Vatican on Monday, with Leo presiding over six private audiences, including with the head of the U.S. military chaplains, Archbishop Timothy Broglio, and one group audience. He also made three appointments, and the Vatican released a letter he had penned to the outgoing dean of the College of Cardinals.
In the afternoon, he was expected to rejoin a weeklong conference he convened on ministering to families.

Leo’s surgery marks the first major health event of his 17-month pontificate. It was significant because the pope himself revealed the news, in perhaps the most public way possible: at the end of his Sunday noon blessing, with thousands of people in St. Peter’s Square.

The Vatican has for centuries zealously guarded the pope’s health and has often sent out confusing information, or none at all, about papal illnesses. Pope Francis tried to change that by being upfront about his frailties and musing on his eventual death. But even during his pontificate, information was tightly controlled.
Leo’s decision and reveal suggested an unusual level of transparency by the American pope.

A lung nodule is a small abnormal area measuring less than 3 centimeters that sometimes appears on a CT scan of the chest or abdomen. Often, the scans are done to investigate trauma or a lung infection, unrelated to a lung cancer screening. A nodule can be benign or malignant, and oftentimes surgical removal is recommended to ascertain whether it is cancerous since performing a lung biopsy by needle can be difficult.
Oncologists say that if the nodule turns out to be cancerous, Leo’s prognosis is “excellent” since it will have been removed at an early stage.

articles.title: Suspected arson attack destroys four cars at prison car park

paras.en: Police were called to the car park at Yatala Labour Prison in Adelaide's north this morning.
Four cars at the site were destroyed by fire in what is being treated as a possible arson attack.
The union representing prison staff is calling for improved security, and the department says all options are on the table.
Four cars have been destroyed by fire at the Yatala Labour Prison car park in Adelaide's north, in what is being investigated as a suspected arson attack.
The early morning incident has prompted renewed calls for enhanced safety at the site from the union representing prison staff, which said its members felt "absolutely outraged" by what had occurred.
The Public Service Association (PSA) said two staff had encountered a person wearing a balaclava when they arrived for work this morning, but the person fled the scene.
"We've got major security concerns and safety concerns for the Yatala car park being wide open like it is," PSA SA vice-president Craig Bates told 891 ABC Adelaide.
"We have been calling on the department to erect a fence."
Police are investigating the incident and have described it as "suspicious", and said emergency services were called to the site on Peter Brown Drive at Northfield about 4am.
They said two Mitsubishi station wagons and two Toyota sedans were completely destroyed.
Police have asked anyone who witnessed suspicious behaviour in the area or has relevant dash cam footage to contact Crime Stoppers.
Department for Correctional Services chief executive David Brown said there was CCTV of the incident, but he would not go into the details of what it showed.
He said he had met with management at the site this morning.
"We've had a critical incident at the site," Mr Brown said.
"It's obviously a live and very active police investigation and we are always looking at ways we can enhance safety for our staff, including the safety of the car park area.
"It was an outrageous incident this morning — four government vehicles were set alight and have been written off by this act of arson. I'm very concerned about the nature of the incident."
The PSA said it had raised concerns five months ago, saying that "inadequate security was putting staff at risk".

The union said it wrote to the department in May urging security improvements including "an extension of the perimeter fence and 24-hour protective security officers", but those requests were rejected.
"Only a number of months ago, a stolen vehicle was driven through that car park with people wearing masks and they were later found to have a firearm," Mr Bates said.
"There have been other issues with vehicles being damaged and stuff like that too.
"A fence is a bit of a no-brainer and it's high time it happened. To be honest it should have happened ages ago."
Mr Brown said the incident would be reviewed, and did not rule out the installation of a new fence.

"Every option is on the table including whether we can partition or fence off access to the car park, but also recognising that Yatala Labour Prison is a large prison and it has a lot of interface with the public," he said.
