articles.title: 'It could have been a very different history': Researchers are finally starting to pin down how many Indigenous people were living in the Americas when Columbus arrived
articles.author: Kristina Killgrove

paras.en: When Christopher Columbus made landfall in the Americas on Oct. 12, 1492, he encountered Indigenous Lucayans living on the Bahamian island now called San Salvador. Columbus wrote in his diary about "great multitudes of men" who greeted him that day, bartered with him and told him about other groups who lived on nearby islands.
paras.zh: 1492 年 10 月 12 日，克里斯托弗·哥伦布 (Christopher Columbus) 在美洲登陆时，遇到了居住在巴哈马岛屿（现称为圣萨尔瓦多）上的土著卢卡亚人。哥伦布在日记中写道，那天有“大量的人”向他致意，与他进行物物交换，并告诉他居住在附近岛屿上的其他群体的情况。

paras.en: But within a few decades after Columbus' arrival, the Indigenous people of the Americas were decimated by what anthropologist Eric Wolf called the "Great Dying" — a combination of epidemic disease, warfare and enslavement that led to a rapid decline in the Native population.
paras.zh: 但在哥伦布抵达后的几十年内，美洲原住民遭受了人类学家埃里克·沃尔夫所说的“大灭绝”的摧残——流行病、战争和奴役的结合导致了原住民人口的迅速下降。

paras.en: For centuries, researchers have been trying to figure out how many Indigenous people lived in the Americas just prior to the fateful arrival of European colonizers.
paras.zh: 几个世纪以来，研究人员一直试图弄清楚在欧洲殖民者到来之前有多少原住民生活在美洲。

paras.en: The answer to that question has been surprisingly elusive, and estimates based on historical censuses, archaeological sites and land carrying capacity in the Western Hemisphere have varied wildly.
paras.zh: 这个问题的答案令人惊讶地难以捉摸，而且基于历史人口普查、考古遗址和西半球土地承载能力的估计差异很大。

paras.en: Recent research into Native American demography has revealed that the population peaked several centuries before Europeans showed up on the shores of North America — and that if Europeans had arrived at that peak, the entire history of the continent may have been different.
paras.zh: 最近对美洲原住民人口统计的研究表明，人口在欧洲人出现在北美海岸之前几个世纪达到顶峰，如果欧洲人到达那个顶峰，整个大陆的历史可能会有所不同。

paras.en: Early estimates of the Indigenous population
paras.zh: 原住民人口的早期估计

paras.en: People have lived in the Americas for at least 14,000 years, having entered the continents via the region around the Bering Strait. Archaeological evidence shows these first Americans dispersed throughout the newly encountered lands fairly quickly. But what happened to the population between that dispersal and the arrival of Columbus is a huge unknown; estimates of the number of Indigenous people living in the Western Hemisphere in 1492 have ranged from 1 million to 112 million people.
paras.zh: 人们在美洲生活了至少 14,000 年，通过白令海峡周围地区进入大陆。考古证据表明，这些第一批美国人很快就分散到了新发现的土地上。但从这次分散到哥伦布到来之间，人口发生了什么仍然是一个巨大的未知数。据估计，1492 年居住在西半球的原住民人数为 100 万至 1.12 亿。

paras.en: "We don't have good quantitative estimates," George Milner, an anthropologist at Penn State, told Live Science. "The numbers are all over the place."
paras.zh: “我们没有很好的定量估计，”宾夕法尼亚州立大学的人类学家乔治·米尔纳告诉《生活科学》。 “数字到处都是。”

paras.en: One of the first modern researchers who attempted to quantify the Indigenous population prior to Columbus was anthropologist Henry Dobyns. In a 1983 book, Dobyns used estimates of how many people each type of landscape could support as well as historical records of 16th-century disease epidemics to arrive at an Indigenous population estimate of around 112 million people — more than 100 times larger than some previous experts had believed.
paras.zh: 在哥伦布之前，最早尝试量化土著人口的现代研究人员之一是人类学家亨利·多宾斯。在 1983 年的一本书中，多宾斯使用了每种类型的景观可以容纳多少人口的估计以及 16 世纪疾病流行的历史记录，得出了大约 1.12 亿人的土著人口估计——比一些以前的专家认为的要多 100 倍以上。

paras.en: "In essence, Dobyns filled up the landscape to its maximum carrying capacity, so that all environmentally similar places were occupied by the same number of people," Milner said. "He also made the assumption that epidemic disease spread widely and universally, which would make sense if the landscape was filled up."
paras.zh: 米尔纳说：“本质上，多宾斯将景观填满到其最大承载能力，以便所有环境相似的地方都被相同数量的人占据。” “他还假设流行病广泛且普遍地传播，如果景观被填满的话，这是有道理的。”

paras.en: But a burst of archaeological research in the 1970s and 1980s revealed that the Americas were not uniformly settled, Milner said. Dobyns' estimates were therefore much too high.
paras.zh: 但米尔纳说，20 世纪 70 年代和 80 年代的一系列考古研究表明，美洲并没有统一的定居点。因此，多宾斯的估计太高了。

paras.en: Researchers then began to focus on creating population estimates for specific regions of the hemisphere, using techniques such as the relative density of pottery sherds at a site, the number of stone tools and flakes, the number and size of houses, and mortality trends from human skeletons.
paras.zh: 然后，研究人员开始专注于对半球特定区域的人口进行估计，使用的技术包括某个地点陶片的相对密度、石器和石片的数量、房屋的数量和大小以及人类骨骼的死亡率趋势。

paras.en: In a 2019 study, geographers compiled 129 population estimates from 82 published studies to model the hemisphere-wide distribution of the Indigenous population in 1492. The researchers split the hemisphere into seven regions — the Caribbean, Mexico, Central America, Inca territory, Amazonia, North America and the rest of the Americas — and reached a combined estimate of 60.5 million. Their estimate for North America (modern-day Canada and the U.S.) was about 3 million to 6 million, less than one-third of Dobyns' estimate of 18 million.
paras.zh: 在 2019 年的一项研究中，地理学家从 82 项已发表的研究中汇总了 129 项人口估计数，以模拟 1492 年原住民人口在半球的分布情况。研究人员将半球分为七个区域——加勒比海、墨西哥、中美洲、印加领土、亚马逊流域、北美和美洲其他地区——并得出总计 6050 万人口的估计值。他们对北美（现在的加拿大和美国）的估计约为 300 万至 600 万，不到多宾斯估计的 1800 万的三分之一。

paras.en: The 2019 study found that the most populous groups in the Western Hemisphere in 1492 were the Aztecs, largely in modern-day Mexico; and the Inca, who lived along the west coast of South America.
paras.zh: 2019 年的研究发现，1492 年西半球人口最多的群体是阿兹特克人，主要分布在今天的墨西哥；以及居住在南美洲西海岸的印加人。

paras.en: But the people we know the most about from an archaeological standpoint are Indigenous groups in the U.S. and Canada.
paras.zh: 但从考古学的角度来看，我们最了解的人是美国和加拿大的土著群体。

paras.en: In a 2010 study, Milner and geographer George Chaplin zoomed in on the data from eastern North America, compiling historic group sizes and sizes of archaeological occupation areas to estimate the location and size of "population aggregates." Using this method, their overall estimate for the eastern U.S. and southeastern Canada was about 1.6 million people.
paras.zh: 在 2010 年的一项研究中，米尔纳和地理学家乔治·卓别林放大了北美东部的数据，编制了历史群体规模和考古占领区的规模，以估计“人口总量”的位置和规模。使用这种方法，他们对美国东部和加拿大东南部的总体估计人口约为 160 万人。

paras.en: "Our mean estimates," Milner and Chaplin wrote, "indicate that North America held roughly 2.8 to 5.7 million people" or a "best estimate" of 3.8 million people in the early 16th century, before European diseases dramatically decreased the size of the Indigenous population.
paras.zh: 米尔纳和卓别林写道，“我们的平均估计表明，在欧洲疾病导致原住民人口规模大幅减少之前，16 世纪初，北美大约有 2.8 至 570 万人”，或者“最佳估计”为 380 万人。

paras.en: "If you want to start estimating specific populations, you should use measures that work across regions," Robert Kelly, an archaeologist at the University of Wyoming, told Live Science. "People produce things that can be carbon-dated everywhere, because everyone had to build fires for heat and for cooking."
paras.zh: 怀俄明大学的考古学家罗伯特·凯利告诉《生活科学》杂志：“如果你想开始估计特定的人口，你应该使用跨地区有效的措施。” “人们生产的东西可以在任何地方进行碳测年，因为每个人都必须生火取暖和做饭。”

paras.en: Charcoal from hearths is one of the main human-made things that archaeologists use to radiocarbon-date a site. The radiocarbon data provides a range of dates showing when the firewood was likeliest to have been used.
paras.zh: 壁炉中的木炭是考古学家用来对遗址进行放射性碳测年的主要人造物品之一。放射性碳数据提供了一系列日期，显示木柴最有可能被使用的时间。

paras.en: In North America, many of those carbon-14 dates from charcoal, as well as from animal bones and plant remains from archaeological sites, have been entered into the Canadian Archaeological Radiocarbon Database (CARD).
paras.zh: 在北美，许多来自木炭以及考古遗址的动物骨骼和植物遗骸的碳 14 年代已被输入加拿大考古放射性碳数据库 (CARD)。

paras.en: In a 2009 study, Matthew Peros, a geographer at Bishop's University in Quebec, and co-authors mathematically combined the radiocarbon date ranges in CARD to generate a single curve that revealed how common C-14 dates were over time. At the time, CARD had about 25,000 records.
paras.zh: 在 2009 年的一项研究中，魁北克主教大学的地理学家 Matthew Peros 和合著者以数学方式组合了 CARD 中的放射性碳日期范围，生成了一条曲线，揭示了 C-14 日期随时间变化的常见程度。当时，CARD 拥有大约 25,000 条记录。

paras.en: Because time periods with more people most likely produced more material that could be carbon-dated, the shape of the radiocarbon date curve gave the team an idea of when the population of North America increased and decreased.
paras.zh: 由于人口越多的时间段很可能产生更多可进行碳测年的物质，放射性碳测年曲线的形状让研究小组了解了北美人口何时增加和减少。

paras.en: They found that the population of North America increased rapidly around 50 B.C. and peaked around A.D. 1150. From that time until European contact, the Indigenous population may have been declining, possibly because of increased mortality from diseases like tuberculosis as people aggregated into denser settlements.
paras.zh: 他们发现北美人口在公元前 50 年左右迅速增加。并在公元 1150 年左右达到顶峰。从那时起直到欧洲人接触，土著人口可能一直在下降，这可能是因为随着人们聚集到更密集的定居点，结核病等疾病的死亡率增加。

paras.en: "The 1150 date was an interesting finding that also surprised us," Peros told Live Science. "I had assumed it would be more like 1500 just following the arrival of the Europeans."
paras.zh: “1150 年是一个有趣的发现，也让我们感到惊讶，”佩罗斯告诉《Live Science》。 “我原以为欧洲人到来后，数量会增加到 1500 左右。”

paras.en: In a 2025 study, Kelly and co-authors found a similar temporal peak. By that time, CARD's dataset had ballooned to over 100,000 dates, making the estimate more robust.
paras.zh: 在 2025 年的一项研究中，凯利和合著者发现了类似的时间峰值。到那时，CARD 的数据集已激增至超过 100,000 个日期，使得估计更加可靠。

paras.en: "Although devastated by European contact, the Indigenous population did not simply increase to a peak at 1500 CE and then decline," the researchers wrote in the study. In fact, they found evidence for a slight recovery in population numbers just prior to 1500.
paras.zh: 研究人员在研究报告中写道：“尽管受到欧洲人接触的破坏，土著人口并没有简单地在公元 1500 年达到顶峰，然后下降。”事实上，他们发现了 1500 年前人口数量略有回升的证据。

paras.en: But how large was that population? By combining the radiocarbon date curve with a starting population and factoring in average annual population growth, researchers can estimate the number of people living in North America around 1492, Peros said.
paras.zh: 但这个人口有多少？佩罗斯说，通过将放射性碳测年曲线与起始人口相结合，并考虑到年平均人口增长因素，研究人员可以估计 1492 年左右生活在北美的人口数量。

paras.en: In their study, Peros and co-authors assumed that a handful of extended families — around 1,000 people — entered North America about 15,000 years ago as the founder population. With those inputs, the researchers estimated that the maximum population of North America was about 2.5 million in 1150 and had declined to about 1.8 million in 1492. But if people arrived significantly earlier than 15,000 years ago — which might be the case, given evidence from sites like White Sands in New Mexico, which dates to 23,000 years ago — or arrived in greater numbers, those population figures would be even higher.
paras.zh: 在他们的研究中，佩罗斯和合著者假设少数大家庭（大约 1,000 人）在大约 15,000 年前作为创始人人口进入北美。根据这些数据，研究人员估计，1150 年北美人口最多约为 250 万，到 1492 年已下降至约 180 万。但如果人们到达的时间明显早于 15,000 年前（新墨西哥州白沙遗址的证据可追溯到 23,000 年前，情况可能就是这样），或者到达的人数更多，那么人口数字会更高。

paras.en: "Had Europeans tried settling the continent at A.D. 1000, they would have run into a much, much larger Indigenous population," Kelly said. At that time, the city of Cahokia, near modern-day St. Louis, encompassed 6 square miles (16 square kilometers) and had a population of nearly 20,000 people.
paras.zh: 凯利说：“如果欧洲人在公元 1000 年试图在这片大陆定居，他们就会遇到数量大得多的土著人口。”当时，卡霍基亚市靠近现代的圣路易斯，面积 6 平方英里（16 平方公里），人口近 20,000 人。

paras.en: "They could have fielded thousands of warriors, and it would have been a very different experience for the Europeans," Kelly said. "It could have been a very different history."
paras.zh: 凯利说：“他们本可以派出数千名战士，这对欧洲人来说将是一次非常不同的经历。” “这可能是一段非常不同的历史。”

paras.en: - 13,000-year-old butchered bones of long-tusked beast found in Chile give more evidence of early first Americans
paras.zh: - 在智利发现的 13,000 年前被屠宰的长牙兽骨头为早期第一批美洲人提供了更多证据

paras.en: - Ancient DNA reveals mysterious Indigenous lineage that lived in Argentina for nearly 8,500 years — but rarely interacted with others
paras.zh: - 古代 DNA 揭示了在阿根廷生活了近 8,500 年但很少与他人互动的神秘土著血统

paras.en: - Ancient Indigenous lineage of Blackfoot Confederacy goes back 18,000 years to last ice age, DNA reveals
paras.zh: - DNA 揭示，黑脚邦联的古代土著血统可以追溯到 18,000 年前的最后一个冰河时代

paras.en: Experts told Live Science that the pre-1492 population of what is now the U.S. and Canada was between 2 million and 4 million. The archaeological deep dive in this region sets up the possibility that a full Western Hemisphere population estimate may be made someday.
paras.zh: 专家告诉《Live Science》，1492 年之前，现在的美国和加拿大人口在 200 万到 400 万之间。该地区的考古深入研究奠定了有一天可能对西半球人口进行全面估计的可能性。

paras.en: Milner is optimistic they'll eventually get there. "Will it be done in my lifetime? Probably not," he said. "It's time-consuming, laborious and not especially flashy work to do."
paras.zh: 米尔纳乐观地认为他们最终会实现这一目标。 “这会在我有生之年完成吗？可能不会，”他说。 “这是一项耗时、费力、而且不是特别华而不实的工作。”

paras.en: Nonetheless, demography is important work, he said, because it can help us make estimates to prepare for the future.
paras.zh: 尽管如此，他说，人口统计学仍然是重要的工作，因为它可以帮助我们做出估计，为未来做好准备。

paras.en: "The world's population has more than doubled in my lifetime; that's unheard of in human existence," Milner said. "Environmental scientists are really trying to look at what's happened over long periods of time to give us a range of variation of what might happen in the future. We have to make some informed decisions about how to manage our landscape and accommodate these changes."
paras.zh: 米尔纳说：“在我一生中，世界人口增加了一倍多；这在人类存在中是闻所未闻的。” “环境科学家确实在努力研究长时间内发生的情况，以便为我们提供未来可能发生的一系列变化。我们必须就如何管理我们的景观和适应这些变化做出一些明智的决定。”

paras.en: Understanding the number of Indigenous inhabitants in the Western Hemisphere in 1492 is also key to understanding the history of North America.
paras.zh: 了解 1492 年西半球土著居民的数量也是了解北美历史的关键。

paras.en: "North America was not an empty continent when the Europeans arrived," Peros said. "There were people and civilizations pretty much everywhere in the Americas for a long period of time. It is important for people to understand that when we talk about questions of reconciliation and when we do land acknowledgements."
paras.zh: “当欧洲人到达时，北美并不是一片空旷的大陆，”佩罗斯说。 “很长一段时间以来，美洲几乎到处都有人和文明。当我们谈论和解问题以及当我们进行土地承认时，人们必须理解这一点，这一点很重要。”

paras.en: Help us improve Live Science Pro: We're always trying to make our content better. Leave us feedback about Pro here.
paras.zh: 帮助我们改进 Live Science Pro：我们一直在努力让我们的内容变得更好。请在此处给我们留下有关 Pro 的反馈。

paras.en: How much do you know about the first people to reach the Americas? Find out with our First Americans quiz!
paras.zh: 您对第一批到达美洲的人了解多少？通过我们的第一批美国人测验来找出答案！

paras.en: Kristina Killgrove is a staff writer at Live Science with a focus on archaeology and paleoanthropology news. Her articles have also appeared in venues such as Forbes, Smithsonian, and Mental Floss. Kristina holds a Ph.D. in biological anthropology and an M.A. in classical archaeology from the University of North Carolina, as well as a B.A. in Latin from the University of Virginia, and she was formerly a university professor and researcher. She has received awards from the Society for American Archaeology and the American Anthropological Association for her science writing.
paras.zh: 克里斯蒂娜·基尔格罗夫 (Kristina Killgrove) 是《Live Science》的特约撰稿人，专注于考古学和古人类学新闻。她的文章还发表在《福布斯》、《史密森尼》和《Mental Floss》等杂志上。克里斯蒂娜拥有博士学位。北卡罗来纳大学生物人类学学士学位和古典考古学硕士学位，以及北卡罗来纳大学古典考古学学士学位。她拥有弗吉尼亚大学拉丁语学位，曾任大学教授和研究员。她因其科学写作而获得美国考古学会和美国人类学协会颁发的奖项。

articles.title: Thieves Pulled Off Another Shocking Art Heist in France. This Time, They Took a 330-Pound Bronze Book Cover Designed by Salvador Dalí

paras.en: Another flagrant museum heist has rocked France. On Sunday night or Monday morning, thieves stole an enormous bronze book cover designed by Salvador Dalí from a small contemporary art collection in the town of Issoire in central France.
paras.zh: 另一起明目张胆的博物馆抢劫案震惊了法国。周日晚上或周一早上，窃贼从法国中部伊苏瓦尔镇的一个小型当代艺术收藏品中偷走了萨尔瓦多·达利设计的巨大青铜书籍封面。

paras.en: The cover belongs to a massive book titled Livre de l’Apocalypse. The work was the collective achievement of seven artists and seven writers who, between 1958 and 1961, were recruited by French publisher Joseph Forêt to interpret and illustrate parts of the Book of Revelation, the canonical last book of the New Testament. These leading creatives—including Ossip Zadkine, Léonard Foujita, Jean Cocteau and Jean Giono—contributed 150 scroll-sized pages of text and biblical scenes that took more than 2,000 hours to complete, according to the Telegraph’s Henry Samuel.
paras.zh: 该封面属于一本名为《启示录》的巨著。该作品是七位艺术家和七位作家的集体成就，他们在 1958 年至 1961 年间被法国出版商 Joseph Forêt 招募，负责解释和插图《新约圣经》最后一本书《启示录》的部分内容。据《每日电讯报》的 Henry Samuel 报道，这些顶尖创意人士——包括 Ossip Zadkine、Léonard Foujita、Jean Cocteau 和 Jean Giono——贡献了 150 页卷轴大小的文本和圣经场景，花了 2000 多个小时才完成。

paras.en: Dalí’s cover leaves a fittingly grand first impression. He created it using a now-lost wax casting technique. Featuring a prominent crucifix, it is made from a constellation of materials, including bronze, gemstones, pearls, forks and seashells. Considered the most expensive book in the world at the time of its creation, the work is likewise famed for its enormous heft. It weighs roughly 463 pounds, with the cover alone tipping the scales at 330 pounds.
paras.zh: 达利的封面给人留下了恰如其分的宏伟第一印象。他使用现已失传的蜡铸造技术创造了它。它以突出的十字架为特色，由多种材料制成，包括青铜、宝石、珍珠、叉子和贝壳。该书在创作时被认为是世界上最昂贵的书，同样因其巨大的分量而闻名。它重约 463 磅，仅盖子重达 330 磅。

paras.en: “It is a monumental work, a masterpiece, unique in the world,” Christian Karoutzos, the book’s owner, who runs an art restoration company and contemporary art gallery in Issoire, tells Olivier Vidal and Christelle Marquès of ICI Pays d’Auvergne, a French radio station. “France was murdered last night. French heritage was murdered.”
paras.zh: “这是一部不朽的作品，一部杰作，在世界上独一无二，”这本书的主人克里斯蒂安·卡鲁佐斯（Christian Karoutzos）在伊苏瓦尔经营着一家艺术修复公司和当代艺术画廊，他告诉法国 ICI Pays d’Auvergne 广播电台的奥利维尔·维达尔（Olivier Vidal）和克里斯泰尔·马奎斯（Christelle Marquès）。 “法国昨晚被谋杀了。法国传统被谋杀了。”

paras.en: The book’s cover and several parchments were on display at Karoutzos’ small private contemporary art center when an unknown number of thieves forced their way through an exterior gate and demolished the book’s plexiglass display case. “They arrived like vandals. They smashed everything,” Karoutzos tells La Montagne’s David Allignon.
paras.zh: 这本书的封面和几张羊皮纸正在卡鲁佐斯的小型私人当代艺术中心展出，当时数量不详的窃贼闯入外门，拆毁了这本书的有机玻璃展示柜。 “他们像破坏者一样到来。他们砸碎了一切，”卡鲁佐斯告诉《蒙塔涅报》的大卫·阿利尼翁。

paras.en: Though all of the book’s parchments were left untouched, authorities remain baffled as to how the theft of such a heavy artwork was carried out so seamlessly.
paras.zh: 尽管这本书的所有羊皮纸都没有被碰过，但当局仍然困惑于如何如此天衣无缝地盗窃如此沉重的艺术品。

paras.en: Valued at 2 million francs at the time of its creation—about $408,000 in 1961 dollars and $4.5 million in today’s money—the book is considered priceless by many for its history and cultural significance. Issoire Mayor Bertrand Barraud described it as “the work of a lifetime” and called its loss “incalculable,” according to Euronews’ Christina Molle.
paras.zh: 这本书在创作时价值 200 万法郎（以 1961 年美元计算约为 408,000 美元，以今天的货币计算为 450 万美元），因其历史和文化意义而被许多人认为是无价之宝。据欧洲新闻台的克里斯蒂娜·莫尔报道，伊苏瓦尔市市长伯特兰·巴罗称其为“一生的工作”，并称其损失“无法估量”。

paras.en: “It has significant artistic value in and of itself, far greater than the individual value of each of the objects that make it up,” Jean-Christophe Castelain, editor-in-chief of the Journal des Arts, tells France24 in a translated interview. “What thief would be interested in an object that weighs 210 kilos? I’ll leave that question open.”
paras.zh: 《艺术杂志》主编让-克里斯托夫·卡斯特兰 (Jean-Christophe Castelain) 在翻译后的采访中告诉 France24：“它本身就具有重要的艺术价值，远远大于构成它的每件物品的个体价值。” “哪个小偷会对重 210 公斤的物体感兴趣？我不会回答这个问题。”

paras.en: For more than a decade after its completion in 1961, the book toured nearly 150 exhibitions around the world, including a stop at the French pavilion at the 1964 World’s Fair in Queens, New York.
paras.zh: 该书于 1961 年完成后的十多年来，在世界各地举办了近 150 个展览，其中包括在 1964 年纽约皇后区世界博览会的法国馆停留。

paras.en: “On exhibit will be a huge quarter‐ton volume, L’Apocalypse, a French translation of the Revelation of St. John the Divine,” the New York Times’ Walter Carlson reported at the time. “The volume was insured for $1 million for its trip from France. Admission will be charged to see it.”
paras.zh: “展出的将是一本重达四分之一吨的巨著《启示录》，这是《圣约翰启示录》的法文译本，”《纽约时报》的沃尔特·卡尔森当时报道道。 “该书从法国出发的旅程已投保 100 万美元。观看该作品需付费。”

paras.en: - The Unisphere, a giant stainless steel globe sculpture that was designed by Gilmore D. Clarke for the 1964 World’s Fair, is still visible at Flushing Meadows Corona Park in Queens.
paras.zh: - Unisphere 是一座巨大的不锈钢地球仪雕塑，由吉尔莫·D·克拉克 (Gilmore D. Clarke) 为 1964 年世界博览会设计，如今在皇后区的法拉盛梅多斯可乐娜公园 (Flushing Meadows Corona Park) 中仍然可见。

paras.en: - At its dedication ceremony, New York City planner Robert Moses said the Unisphere was “built to remain as a permanent feature of the park, reminding succeeding generations of a pageant of surpassing interest and significance.”
paras.zh: - 在落成仪式上，纽约市规划师罗伯特·摩西表示，大地球仪“的建造是为了作为公园的永久特色，提醒后代这是一场具有超越意义和意义的盛会。”

paras.en: Karoutzos bought the massive book in 2003 for “several million euros,” as he tells Le Figaro’s Alix Vermande. The tome’s previous owners had intended to divide it up and sell the separate pieces.
paras.zh: 卡鲁佐斯在 2003 年以“几百万欧元”的价格买下了这本巨著，他告诉《费加罗报》的阿利克斯·维芒德 (Alix Vermande)。这本书的前主人打算将其分割并出售单独的部分。

paras.en: The heist is the latest in a series of high-profile art thefts carried out across Europe in the past few months. In September, thieves stole four Pierre-Auguste Renoir paintings worth an estimated $2.5 million from a museum on the French Riviera. In August, 3,000-year-old Bronze Age artifacts were looted from Villena, Spain; that same month, four Renaissance works by Antonello da Messina were taken from a museum in Sicily.
paras.zh: 这起盗窃案是过去几个月欧洲各地发生的一系列备受瞩目的艺术品盗窃案中的最新一起。 9 月，窃贼从法国里维埃拉的一家博物馆偷走了四幅皮埃尔·奥古斯特·雷诺阿的画作，估计价值 250 万美元。 8 月，西班牙维耶纳 (Villena) 的 3000 年前青铜器时代文物被洗劫一空；同月，安东内罗·达·梅西纳的四件文艺复兴时期作品被从西西里岛的一家博物馆盗走。

articles.title: Flu Season Started Early in Parts of the U.S., and Experts Say You Should Consider Getting the Seasonal Jab ASAP. Here's What to Know

paras.en: Every year, autumn brings gorgeous foliage, crisp air, shorter days—and a slew of respiratory illnesses. Flu season usually starts in October or November, but infection data suggests it has kicked off early in parts of the Northern Hemisphere.
paras.zh: 每年秋天都会带来绚丽的树叶、清新的空气、较短的白天以及一系列呼吸道疾病。流感季节通常在十月或十一月开始，但感染数据显示，在北半球部分地区，流感季节已经提前开始。

paras.en: Flu rates began rising in August or September in many western states, including California, Washington, Alaska and Hawaii. That’s unusual because the respiratory illness typically starts in the Southeast and spreads toward the West Coast. Infection rates have also been unusually early in places like Japan and the United Kingdom.
paras.zh: 在许多西部州，包括加利福尼亚州、华盛顿州、阿拉斯加和夏威夷，流感发病率从八月或九月开始上升。这是不寻常的，因为呼吸道疾病通常始于东南部并向西海岸传播。日本和英国等地的感染率也异常早。

paras.en: We’re “looking at an early flu season this year,” said James Watt, deputy director of infectious diseases at the California Department of Public Health, at a briefing on October 6, reports Catherine Ho at the San Francisco Chronicle.
paras.zh: 据《旧金山纪事报》的凯瑟琳·何 (Catherine Ho) 报道，加州公共卫生部传染病副主任詹姆斯·瓦特 (James Watt) 在 10 月 6 日的新闻发布会上表示，我们“预计今年流感季节会提前”。

paras.en: This early rise is concerning because people haven’t started getting their vaccines yet, says Danielle Zerr, an infectious-diseases specialist at Seattle Children’s, to Lena H. Sun at the Washington Post. “The way flu is circulating now, you wanted that vaccine in you two weeks ago, if not even a little before that.”
paras.zh: 西雅图儿童医院的传染病专家丹妮尔·泽尔 (Danielle Zerr) 向《华盛顿邮报》的莉娜·H·孙 (Lena H. Sun) 表示，这种早期上升令人担忧，因为人们还没有开始接种疫苗。 “按照流感现在的传播方式，你在两周前就需要接种疫苗，甚至更早一点。”

paras.en: Here’s what you need to know about this year’s early flu season.
paras.zh: 以下是您需要了解的有关今年早期流感季节的信息。

paras.en: The flu is caused by an infection with an influenza virus. There are two subtypes of Influenza A—H3N2 and H1N1—and one type of Influenza B, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). The severity of each season depends on which version of the virus is spreading. H3N2 influenza strains are linked to more severe flu seasons and more hospitalizations. This year, the other one, H1N1, is dominating.
paras.zh: 流感是由流感病毒感染引起的。根据美国疾病控制与预防中心 (CDC) 的数据，甲型流感有两种亚型——H3N2 和 H1N1——以及一种乙型流感。每个季节的严重程度取决于正在传播的病毒版本。 H3N2 流感病毒株与更严重的流感季节和更多的住院治疗有关。今年，另一种 H1N1 流感占据主导地位。

paras.en: Flu spreads via droplets spewed when an infected person coughs, sneezes or talks. Symptoms generally appear one to four days after infection. Signs of illness can include fever or feverish chills, cough, sore throat, runny nose, muscle aches and fatigue. A sick individual is most contagious during their first three days of symptoms.
paras.zh: 流感通过感染者咳嗽、打喷嚏或说话时喷出的飞沫传播。症状通常在感染后一到四天出现。疾病迹象可能包括发烧或发烧发冷、咳嗽、喉咙痛、流鼻涕、肌肉酸痛和疲劳。病人在出现症状的前三天最具传染性。

paras.en: Since 2010, the flu has resulted in between 120,000 and 710,000 hospitalizations and has contributed to between 6,300 and 52,000 deaths each year in the U.S., according to estimates by the CDC.
paras.zh: 据美国疾病预防控制中心估计，自 2010 年以来，流感每年在美国导致 120,000 至 710,000 人住院治疗，并导致 6,300 至 52,000 人死亡。

paras.en: Experts don’t know for sure, but one possibility is that a new variant of H1N1 evolved a mutation that is better at evading some people’s immune systems. “That’s our best argument for what’s going on right now in terms of this early flu season,” says Alex Greninger, a virologist at the University of Washington, to Rob Stein at NPR.
paras.zh: 专家们并不确定，但一种可能性是，H1N1 流感的一种新变种进化出了一种突变，能够更好地逃避某些人的免疫系统。华盛顿大学病毒学家亚历克斯·格雷宁格 (Alex Greninger) 对美国公共广播电台 (NPR) 的罗布·斯坦因 (Rob Stein) 表示：“这是我们对当前流感季节早期所发生情况的最佳论据。”

paras.en: Another reason might be that because H3N2 dominated last year’s flu season, people have less recent immunity against the version that’s currently running rampant, Helen Chu, an infectious-diseases specialist at the University of Washington, tells the Washington Post.
paras.zh: 华盛顿大学传染病专家 Helen Chu 告诉《华盛顿邮报》，另一个原因可能是，由于 H3N2 主导了去年的流感季节，人们最近对目前猖獗的 H3N2 病毒的免疫力较低。

paras.en: It’s still too soon to tell what this year’s season will look like. Looking at the Southern Hemisphere can offer clues, since our seasons are flipped, writes Katelyn Jetelina for Your Local Epidemiologist. “Flu season was severe in many places this summer,” she explains, with Argentina recording its highest number of flu-like illness cases in a decade. That doesn’t necessarily mean things will look the same in the Northern Hemisphere, but it’s something epidemiologists are keeping an eye on.
paras.zh: 现在判断今年的季节会是什么样子还为时过早。凯特琳·杰特琳娜为当地流行病学家写道，观察南半球可以提供线索，因为我们的季节交替。她解释说：“今年夏天，许多地方的流感季节都很严重。”阿根廷的流感样疾病病例数创下十年来最高。这并不一定意味着北半球的情况会一样，但流行病学家正在密切关注。

paras.en: What’s more, “an early start doesn’t necessarily mean a more severe season,” says James Hay, an epidemiologist at the University of Oxford in England, to Nature’s Mariana Lenharo.
paras.zh: 此外，英国牛津大学的流行病学家詹姆斯·海伊 (James Hay) 对《自然》杂志的玛丽安娜·伦哈罗 (Mariana Lenharo) 表示，“提早开始并不一定意味着疫情会更加严重”。

paras.en: Flu vaccines for 2026-27 are already available, and the best thing you can do is get your shot as early as possible—even if you got one last year. The vaccine is adjusted every year to target the strains that researchers predict will be circulating that season. While it’s hard for them to get it exactly right, vaccines still offer an important level of protection that can reduce the severity of the illness.
paras.zh: 2026-27 年流感疫苗已经上市，您能做的最好的事情就是尽早接种疫苗——即使您去年接种过疫苗。该疫苗每年都会进行调整，以针对研究人员预测将在该季节传播的菌株。虽然他们很难做到完全正确，但疫苗仍然提供了重要的保护水平，可以减轻疾病的严重程度。

paras.en: “This is one of those seasons where the key message is to go get vaccinated now,” Greninger tells Nature.
paras.zh: 格雷宁格告诉《自然》杂志：“这是关键信息是立即接种疫苗的季节之一。”

articles.title: Just Inches Below the Forest Floor, Archaeologists in Germany Unearthed a Roman Temple Likely Dedicated to Mars, the God of War

paras.en: Archaeologists in Germany have discovered the remains of a Roman temple that appears to have been dedicated to Mars, the god of war.
paras.zh: 德国考古学家发现了一座罗马神庙的遗迹，这座神庙似乎是供奉战神马尔斯的。

paras.en: The structure was concealed just beneath the forest floor in the foothills of the eastern Taunus Mountains, on the northern outskirts of Frankfurt, according to a September 25 announcement from the Hesse State Office for Monument Preservation.
paras.zh: 根据黑森州纪念碑保护办公室 9 月 25 日的公告，该建筑隐藏在法兰克福北郊陶努斯山脉东部山麓的森林地面下方。

paras.en: The temple is rectangular and measures about 16 feet long. Inside, it appears to have contained a smaller, square chamber with just three roughly 20-inch-thick walls, Thomas Kurella reports for Hessenschau. Archaeologists believe the structure could be an ambulatory temple, with the three-walled central prayer room accessible through a wooden gate or door and surrounded by covered walkways.
paras.zh: 寺庙呈长方形，长约16英尺。托马斯·库雷拉 (Thomas Kurella) 为 Hessenschau 报道称，里面似乎包含一个较小的方形房间，只有三层大约 20 英寸厚的墙壁。考古学家认为，该建筑可能是一座流动寺庙，其三墙中央祈祷室可通过木门或门进入，周围环绕着有盖的走道。

paras.en: Researchers found an inscription suggesting that the temple was dedicated to Mars, according to Live Science’s Kristina Killgrove. They also unearthed a fragment of a statue that may have portrayed the war god. Another statuette likely represents Victoria, the Roman goddess of victory who often appears alongside Mars and was worshipped by the Roman military. The artifact is broken, but it still clearly bears the hallmarks of Victoria: wings, a palm branch and a laurel wreath, per Hessenschau.
paras.zh: 据《Live Science》的克里斯蒂娜·基尔格罗夫称，研究人员发现了一段铭文，表明这座神庙是献给火星的。他们还出土了可能描绘战神的雕像的碎片。另一尊小雕像很可能代表罗马胜利女神维多利亚，她经常与玛尔斯一起出现，并受到罗马军队的崇拜。这件文物已破损，但仍清晰地带有维多利亚的标志：翅膀、棕榈树枝和月桂花环（根据 Hessenschau 的说法）。

paras.en: Archaeologists unearthed this temple during ongoing excavations of the Kapersburg fort—a Roman military fortification thought to date back to the second century C.E.—and its neighboring village, known as a “vicus,” which likely housed the soldiers’ families, merchants and other civilians.
paras.zh: 考古学家在卡珀斯堡堡垒（据认为可以追溯到公元二世纪的罗马军事防御工事）及其邻近的村庄（被称为“vicus”）的持续挖掘过程中发现了这座寺庙，该村庄可能居住着士兵的家人、商人和其他平民。

paras.en: The fort was likely constructed under the reign of Emperor Trajan or Emperor Hadrian, per Live Science. A Roman military unit called the Numerus Nidensium was stationed there for roughly 150 years, until the fort was abandoned in the middle of the third century C.E. The group likely originated in the nearby Roman town of Nida, now the Heddernheim quarter of Frankfurt.
paras.zh: 据《Live Science》报道，这座堡垒很可能是在图拉真皇帝或哈德良皇帝统治时期建造的。一支名为“Numerus Nidensium”的罗马军事单位驻扎在那里大约 150 年，直到公元三世纪中叶该堡垒被废弃。该组织可能起源于附近的罗马城镇奈达，即现在的法兰克福海德海姆区。

paras.en: Researchers believe roughly 160 men were stationed at the fort, while up to 700 people lived in the nearby village, per Hessenschau.
paras.zh: 据 Hessenschau 报道，研究人员认为这座堡垒驻扎了大约 160 人，附近村庄则居住着多达 700 人。

paras.en: The site is part of the Upper Germanic-Rhaetian Limes, which became a UNESCO World Heritage site in 2005. This 342-mile stretch, which runs between the Rhine and the Danube rivers, formed part of the Roman Empire’s border, marking not only its military frontier but also the limits of its economic and cultural influence.
paras.zh: 该遗址是上日耳曼-雷蒂亚界线的一部分，于 2005 年成为联合国教科文组织世界遗产。这条 342 英里的河段横跨莱茵河和多瑙河，是罗马帝国边界的一部分，不仅标志着其军事边界，也标志着其经济和文化影响力的界限。

paras.en: Archaeologists have been excavating the fort for decades. However, they recently turned their attention toward the adjacent settlement after drought, pests and a storm cleared away some of the surrounding forest.
paras.zh: 几十年来，考古学家一直在挖掘这座堡垒。然而，由于干旱、害虫和暴风雨摧毁了周围的一些森林，他们最近将注意力转向了邻近的定居点。

paras.en: Because of the site’s location in the wooded foothills, it has remained largely untouched for centuries, leaving well-preserved structures and artifacts just beneath the top layer of soil. Previous excavations have unearthed a Roman votive stone, which is now on view at a museum in nearby Rosbach vor der Höhe.
paras.zh: 由于该遗址位于树木繁茂的山麓，几个世纪以来基本上没有受到任何影响，在土壤表层下留下了保存完好的结构和文物。之前的挖掘工作中出土了一块罗马许愿石，目前在 Rosbach vor der Höhe 附近的一家博物馆展出。

paras.en: This year, in addition to the temple, researchers found the remains of craft activities, including blacksmith pits and baking ovens that may have been used for drying grain, per Live Science. They didn’t find as many houses as they had suspected, suggesting that the site once functioned as an interstitial area between the fort and the settlement.
paras.zh: 据《Live Science》报道，今年，除了寺庙之外，研究人员还发现了手工艺活动的遗迹，包括铁匠坑和可能用于干燥谷物的烤炉。他们没有找到像他们怀疑的那样多的房屋，这表明该地点曾经是堡垒和定居点之间的间隙区域。

paras.en: The Romans held two festivals in honor of Mars each year, one in the spring and one in the fall. He was seen as the protector of not only Rome but also the Roman way of life.
paras.zh: 罗马人每年举行两个节日来纪念火星，一个在春天，一个在秋天。他不仅被视为罗马的保护者，也是罗马生活方式的保护者。

paras.en: Next to the recently excavated temple, a piece of jewelry from a later period indicates that the site continued to see use after the Roman military presence dissipated. The archaeologists are currently deciphering a Latin inscription on another votive stone from within the temple chamber, which may reveal further information, or even the name, of the ancient village near the Kapersburg fort.
paras.zh: 在最近出土的寺庙旁边，一件晚期的珠宝表明，在罗马军事存在消失后，该遗址继续被使用。考古学家目前正在破译神庙室内另一块许愿石上的拉丁文铭文，这可能会揭示卡珀斯堡堡垒附近古村庄的更多信息，甚至名称。

articles.title: California’s Tallest and Most Iconic Trees Are Getting Heatstroke
articles.author: Neel Dhanesha

paras.en: This story originally appeared on Vox and is part of the Climate Desk collaboration.
paras.zh: 这个故事最初出现在 Vox 上，是气候台合作的一部分。

paras.en: A grove of coast redwood trees is a forest of forests. Individual trees can live for thousands of years, and as they grow, their canopies develop mats of soils and ferns, creating something like a second forest floor hundreds of feet above the ground.
paras.zh: 海岸红杉树林是森林中的森林。单棵树可以存活数千年，随着它们的生长，它们的树冠会长出土壤和蕨类植物的垫子，形成距离地面数百英尺的第二层森林地面。

paras.en: These elevated ecosystems are home to creatures like the wandering salamander, which can spend its entire life cycle on top of a single tree, and the marbled murrelet, a seabird whose nesting habits were a mystery until one day in 1974, when a tree-trimmer stumbled upon a nest 150 feet above the ground. Sometimes a stray seed—a sitka spruce or oak or even another redwood—finds its way up a massive redwood and grows into another tree entirely, nestled among the branches of a giant.
paras.zh: 这些高地生态系统是诸如流浪蝾螈和大理石海雀等生物的家园，它们的整个生命周期都在一棵树上度过，而大理石海雀是一种海鸟，其筑巢习惯一直是个谜，直到 1974 年的一天，一名树木修剪工偶然发现了一个离地面 150 英尺高的巢穴。有时，一颗散落的种子——锡卡云杉或橡树，甚至其他红杉——会爬上一棵巨大的红杉，完全长成另一棵树，依偎在巨人的树枝间。

paras.en: For millennia, redwoods have been the anchors of this incredibly stable ecosystem; they can even survive wildfires that devastate other tree species. They’ve also been the source of plenty of human inspiration and drive millions of dollars to California’s tourist economy. But like other living things, they aren’t immune to warming temperatures, and it turns out these trees have a particular weak spot.
paras.zh: 几千年来，红杉一直是这个极其稳定的生态系统的支柱。它们甚至可以在摧毁其他树种的野火中幸存下来。它们也是人类大量灵感的源泉，为加州的旅游经济带来了数百万美元的收入。但与其他生物一样，它们也无法免受气温升高的影响，而且事实证明这些树木有一个特殊的弱点。

paras.en: A new study from researchers at the University of California, Davis, using measurements taken twice a month for two years, found that coast redwood leaves essentially dial down their photosynthesis during periods of extreme heat. This means trees are slowing their “breathing” and “eating” because they can’t cool down fast enough when temperatures rise. It’s a problem that’s only going to get worse as climate change continues to drive global temperatures up, and it raises urgent questions about the future of these iconic trees and the layers of life that live on and around their shadow-dappled lengths.
paras.zh: 加州大学戴维斯分校的研究人员进行的一项新研究，在两年内每月进行两次测量，发现海岸红杉树叶在极端炎热的时期基本上会降低其光合作用。这意味着树木正在减慢“呼吸”和“进食”，因为当气温升高时它们无法足够快地冷却。随着气候变化继续推高全球气温，这个问题只会变得更加严重，它引发了人们对这些标志性树木的未来以及生活在它们阴影斑驳的长度上和周围的生命层的紧迫问题。

paras.en: To understand what’s happening to the redwoods—and what that may mean for the species that rely on them—first we need to take a quick foray into tree anatomy. Trees use the pores in their leaves, stomata, to do two things: take carbon dioxide in, and let water out. Open stomata mean the tree is “breathing” in carbon dioxide and photosynthesizing, but probably also letting water out. Closed stomata mean the tree is conserving water but also slowing down its photosynthesis, since it isn’t taking in any carbon dioxide.
paras.zh: 为了了解红杉发生了什么，以及这对依赖它们的物种意味着什么，首先我们需要快速了解树木解剖学。树木利用叶子上的气孔（气孔）做两件事：吸入二氧化碳，排出水分。气孔开放意味着树木正在“呼吸”二氧化碳并进行光合作用，但也可能会释放水分。气孔关闭意味着树木可以保存水分，但也会减慢光合作用，因为它不吸收任何二氧化碳。

paras.en: “Because leaves are a physical, light-absorbing object, they heat up just like asphalt would in the sun,” said Lily Klinek, a PhD student at UC Davis who was the lead author on the study.
paras.zh: 该研究的主要作者、加州大学戴维斯分校的博士生 Lily Klinek 表示：“因为叶子是一种物理的、吸光的物体，它们会像沥青在阳光下一样升温。”

paras.en: “They’re heating up faster than the air around them,” she said. “And one way that they can cope with this is by opening their stomata and allowing water to transpire out of the leaf, which is kind of like the way that humans sweat. When water evaporates off our skin, it cools us down, and it’s the same for leaves. But they can only really do that if they have enough water to lose.”
paras.zh: “它们升温的速度比周围空气的速度还要快，”她说。 “它们应对这一问题的一种方法是打开气孔，让水分从叶子中蒸发出来，这有点像人类出汗的方式。当水从我们的皮肤上蒸发时，我们就会凉爽下来，叶子也是如此。但只有当它们有足够的水分可以流失时，它们才能真正做到这一点。”

paras.en: Klinek and her colleagues studied coast redwoods in Mendocino County, near the southern part of their range, where the researchers used specialized instruments to measure whether or not individual leaves were photosynthesizing. During heat waves, they found, coast redwoods hit a point where they can’t cool down fast enough, and they just keep their stomata closed. While that saves water, it also means the tree isn’t taking in more carbon—which means it’s not “eating” or building up energy stores it can use to keep growing.
paras.zh: 克利内克和她的同事研究了门多西诺县的海岸红杉，靠近其分布范围的南部，研究人员在那里使用专门的仪器来测量单片叶子是否进行光合作用。他们发现，在热浪期间，海岸红杉达到了无法足够快冷却的程度，并且它们只是保持气孔关闭。虽然这可以节省水，但也意味着树不会吸收更多的碳，这意味着它不会“吃”或积累可用于保持生长的能量储存。

paras.en: This may sound like a technicality of tree physiology. But it could have a big impact on these forests, creating a vicious cycle where trees don’t have enough carbon stored to replenish their leaves in the future, which means they won’t be able to photosynthesize as efficiently, which will starve them even further, repeating until trees eventually die. And while this sort of behavior has been observed in tropical trees, it’s the first time anyone has studied how coast redwoods respond to the same heat stress.
paras.zh: 这听起来像是树木生理学的技术细节。但这可能会对这些森林产生重大影响，造成恶性循环，树木没有足够的碳储存来补充未来的叶子，这意味着它们将无法有效地进行光合作用，这将使它们进一步挨饿，如此反复，直到树木最终死亡。虽然在热带树木中观察到了这种行为，但这是第一次有人研究海岸红杉如何应对相同的热应激。

paras.en: “The term people use is carbon starvation,” said Chris Still, a forest ecologist at Oregon State University who didn’t participate in the study. “Leaves can be expensive to build for a plant.”
paras.zh: “人们使用的术语是碳饥饿，”俄勒冈州立大学森林生态学家克里斯·斯蒂尔（Chris Still）说，他没有参与这项研究。 “为植物建造叶子可能会很昂贵。”

paras.en: Most of the redwoods in California and the Pacific Northwest nowadays are new-growth forests planted in the last couple of centuries. That means the trees are relatively hungry, like growing adolescents, compared to their old-growth cousins, so they need to suck in lots of carbon dioxide to grow taller.
paras.zh: 如今，加利福尼亚州和太平洋西北地区的大多数红杉都是过去几个世纪种植的新森林。这意味着，与它们的老树表亲相比，这些树就像正在成长的青少年一样，相对饥饿，因此它们需要吸收大量二氧化碳才能长得更高。

paras.en: Redwoods are also incredibly good at storing carbon. Thanks to their bulk and long lives, they store more carbon dioxide per acre than any other forest in the world. “Not only is it negative feedback on the climate system itself, with less carbon sequestration from these trees and forests, but the trees themselves are going to obviously not grow as big,” said Anthony Ambrose, a plant physiological ecologist and co-founder of the Ancient Forest Society. So even if the trees survive, they might not have as much space for fern and soil mats, which means less habitat for the creatures that live in them, and they may not grow as tall as they once used to, which could hurt them in another way.
paras.zh: 红杉在储存碳方面也非常出色。由于体积庞大且寿命长，它们每英亩储存的二氧化碳比世界上任何其他森林都多。植物生理生态学家、古代森林协会联合创始人安东尼·安布罗斯说：“这不仅对气候系统本身产生负反馈，这些树木和森林的碳固存量减少，而且树木本身显然不会长得那么大。”因此，即使树木存活下来，它们也可能没有足够的空间容纳蕨类植物和土壤垫，这意味着生活在其中的生物的栖息地减少，而且它们可能不会像以前那样长得那么高，这可能会以另一种方式伤害它们。

paras.en: A central threat to these trees, Klinek explained, is that in addition to the heat stress, they may also lose a crucial source of hydration and protection: Coast redwoods have an intricate relationship with the fogs of their native Northern California and the Pacific Northwest. The trees are so tall that their canopies reach high into fog layers, where they can sip water directly from the sky. The fog also shades the trees from the sun and helps coast redwoods create their own microclimate, which is why these forests are noticeably cooler than the areas adjacent to them. But warmer oceans and drier air are making fog more sporadic, which means the trees are missing a crucial source of relief from heat that is only getting more intense.
paras.zh: 克利内克解释说，这些树木面临的主要威胁是，除了热应激之外，它们还可能失去重要的水合作用和保护来源：海岸红杉与其家乡北加州和太平洋西北地区的雾气有着复杂的关系。这些树非常高，树冠高高地延伸到雾层中，它们可以直接从天空汲水。雾还会遮挡树木免受阳光照射，并帮助海岸红杉创造自己的小气候，这就是为什么这些森林比邻近地区明显凉爽的原因。但海洋变暖和空气干燥使得雾变得更加零星，这意味着树木失去了缓解炎热天气的重要来源，而炎热的天气只会变得越来越强烈。

paras.en: “It’s kind of a double whammy,” said Todd Dawson, a plant ecophysiologist at the University of California Berkeley, who also didn’t participate in the study. “They’re running out of water and also getting this heat stress,” he said. “They’re used to living in a very narrow temperature range of 8 to 27 degrees Celsius (about 46 to 80 degrees Fahrenheit). California, like everywhere, has been getting long periods of much warmer days than we’ve ever experienced, and now the fog, which is normally kind of like an air conditioner, has also declined between 30 and 40 percent.”
paras.zh: “这有点双重打击，”加州大学伯克利分校植物生态生理学家托德·道森（Todd Dawson）说，他也没有参与这项研究。 “他们的水即将耗尽，而且还面临着热应激，”他说。 “他们习惯了生活在 8 至 27 摄氏度（约 46 至 80 华氏度）的狭窄温度范围内。与其他地方一样，加州的天气持续了很长一段时间，比我们经历过的要温暖得多，而现在，通常有点像空调的雾气也减少了 30% 至 40%。”

paras.en: These temperature swings also impact the organisms living high up in the trees. “If they experience really excessive heat throughout the summer,” Ambrose said, “then the soil mats and ferns will probably dry out much faster. And then those salamanders and birds might not be able to live there. So we’ll see cascading effects through the whole ecosystem at that point.”
paras.zh: 这些温度波动也会影响生活在高树上的生物体。 “如果它们整个夏天都经历了非常炎热的天气，”安布罗斯说，“那么土壤垫和蕨类植物可能会干燥得更快。然后那些蝾螈和鸟类可能无法在那里生活。所以到那时我们将看到整个生态系统的连锁效应。”

paras.en: Klinek said, the trees seem to be doing okay after the heat passes; while the leaves she and her team looked at over their two-year study didn’t acclimate to the heat, they also didn’t lose their capacity to photosynthesize after the heat passed. While that’s a bit of hopeful news, it doesn’t reduce the urgency of the need to better understand the impact of climate change on these trees, and to reduce the warming itself.
paras.zh: 克利内克说，炎热天气过去后，树木似乎表现良好；虽然她和她的团队在两年的研究中观察到叶子没有适应高温，但在高温过去后它们也没有失去光合作用的能力。虽然这是一个充满希望的消息，但它并没有减少更好地了解气候变化对这些树木的影响以及减少变暖本身的紧迫性。

paras.en: “Right now the temperatures are coming back to normal in the fall and winter and letting the trees recover,” Klinek said. “But in five or 10 years, if temperatures are even hotter and heat waves are even more frequent, we don’t really know if there would be a recovery.”
paras.zh: “现在秋季和冬季气温正在恢复正常，树木也能恢复，”克利内克说。 “但五年或十年后，如果气温更高、热浪更频繁，我们真的不知道是否会复苏。”

paras.en: For now, the salamanders and seabirds still have their homes high atop the coast redwoods. But we’re a part of the redwoods’ larger ecosystem too, even if we don’t live near them—they, like all trees, are key to keeping our planet hospitable. The trees Klinek studied have the potential to live for more than a thousand years. The question is if we’ll let them.
paras.zh: 目前，蝾螈和海鸟的家园仍然位于海岸红杉的高处。但我们也是红杉更大生态系统的一部分，即使我们不住在红杉附近，它们和所有树木一样，是保持我们的星球宜居的关键。克利内克研究的树木有寿命超过一千年的潜力。问题是我们是否会让他们这么做。

articles.title: How the 2026 Super El Niño and Climate Change Are Related
articles.author: Fernanda González

paras.en: The tropical Pacific has seen heat build for months as a “super” El Niño takes shape.
paras.zh: 随着“超级”厄尔尼诺现象的形成，热带太平洋地区的热量已经持续数月。

paras.en: A climate phenomenon that forms every few years, this year’s iteration of El Niño has been on a tear of daily records and is forecast to reach unprecedented strength this winter. While it’s characterized by hotter-than-normal waters in the eastern tropical Pacific, El Niño is a global problem.
paras.zh: 厄尔尼诺现象每隔几年就会出现一次，今年的厄尔尼诺现象刷新了每日记录，预计今年冬天将达到前所未有的强度。虽然厄尔尼诺现象的特点是东部热带太平洋的海水温度高于正常水平，但厄尔尼诺现象却是一个全球性问题。

paras.en: It’s fair to wonder how another global problem is interacting with El Niño: climate change, driven by burning fossil fuels. While a hotter climate begetting a hotter El Niño might seem like a done deal, “I have more questions than I have reactions” to what’s happening, says Christopher Callahan, a climate researcher at Indiana University. In other words, the relationship is still an area of active research—and this year’s event could provide vital insights.
paras.zh: 人们很想知道另一个全球问题如何与厄尔尼诺现象相互作用：由燃烧化石燃料驱动的气候变化。印第安纳大学气候研究员克里斯托弗·卡拉汉表示，虽然气候变暖引发厄尔尼诺现象似乎已成定局，但对正在发生的事情“我的疑问多于反应”。换句话说，这种关系仍然是一个活跃的研究领域，而今年的活动可以提供重要的见解。

paras.en: El Niño’s added ocean heat affects the atmosphere, causing weather patterns around the world to shift. Consider it kind of like a domino run, where one tile starts a chain reaction. Such a major slug of heat in the Pacific will act more like a shove then a light flick on the atmosphere, and the resulting shifts in weather are expected to be generationally intense.
paras.zh: 厄尔尼诺现象增加的海洋热量影响大气，导致世界各地的天气模式发生变化。可以将其视为多米诺骨牌，其中一块瓷砖会引发连锁反应。太平洋上如此大的一股热流对大气层的影响更像是一股推力，而不是轻轻一弹，预计由此产生的天气变化将是一代又一代的强烈变化。

paras.en: The US National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration is forecasting 100 percent odds of an extremely strong El Niño through December and above 80 percent odds it stays that way through February. Data shows this El Niño has already set multiple all-time daily heat records including a recent peak of 3.4 degrees Celsius.
paras.zh: 美国国家海洋和大气管理局预测，12 月份出现极强厄尔尼诺现象的可能性为 100%，并且这种情况持续到 2 月份的可能性超过 80%。数据显示，这次厄尔尼诺现象已经创下了多项历史日最高气温记录，其中包括最近的3.4摄氏度峰值。

paras.en: NOAA issues its El Niño forecast as a three-month rolling average, and the agency predicts heat could peak at 2.7 degrees Celsius above normal for the period from October to December. (It’s not out of the question that heat could surpass 3 degrees Celsius, though.) If the forecast holds true, it would smash the previous record of 2.4 degrees Celsius, which was set during the 1982-1983 event.
paras.zh: NOAA 以三个月滚动平均值的形式发布了厄尔尼诺现象预测，该机构预测 10 月至 12 月期间气温可能会达到比正常水平高 2.7 摄氏度的峰值。 （不过，气温可能超过 3 摄氏度并非不可能。）如果预测属实，它将打破 1982 年至 1983 年赛事期间创下的 2.4 摄氏度的纪录。

paras.en: How Is Climate Change Impacting El Niño?
paras.zh: 气候变化如何影响厄尔尼诺现象？

paras.en: There is a growing body of evidence that climate change is likely playing at least some role in influencing El Niño. The magnitude and frequency of the phenomenon has increased over the past 60 years, says Francisco Estrada, coordinator of the Climate Change Research Program at the National Autonomous University of Mexico, and so has the variability and how the effects are distributed around the world. He says there shouldn’t be a debate framed as a choice between a “natural El Niño” and an “El Niño caused by climate change” but rather as an interaction between the two processes.
paras.zh: 越来越多的证据表明，气候变化可能至少在影响厄尔尼诺现象方面发挥了一定作用。墨西哥国立自治大学气候变化研究项目协调员弗朗西斯科·埃斯特拉达 (Francisco Estrada) 表示，过去 60 年来，这种现象的严重程度和频率有所增加，其变化及其影响在世界各地的分布方式也随之增加。他表示，不应将争论视为“自然厄尔尼诺”和“气候变化引起的厄尔尼诺”之间的选择，而应将其视为两个过程之间的相互作用。

paras.en: “You can’t separate El Niño from global warming—they’re inextricably linked,” he explains.
paras.zh: “你无法将厄尔尼诺现象与全球变暖分开——它们有着千丝万缕的联系，”他解释道。

paras.en: Modeling also indicates that El Niño is likely to strengthen as the planet warms, though Callahan notes that many models struggle to accurately represent long-term temperature trends in the eastern tropical Pacific. That can give researchers some pause, but there’s also other evidence that climate change is juicing El Niño.
paras.zh: 模型还表明，随着地球变暖，厄尔尼诺现象可能会加强，尽管卡拉汉指出，许多模型很难准确地代表东热带太平洋的长期温度趋势。这可能会让研究人员犹豫一下，但还有其他证据表明气候变化正在加剧厄尔尼诺现象。

paras.en: “The majority of climate models say that El Nino amplitude shall go up in a warming climate, and all of our paleoclimate records say that we're currently in a more active period of El Niño than the last several 1,000 years,” Callahan says.
paras.zh: “大多数气候模型都表明，在气候变暖的情况下，厄尔尼诺现象的幅度将会上升，而我们所有的古气候记录都表明，我们目前正处于厄尔尼诺现象比过去几千年更加活跃的时期，”卡拉汉说。

paras.en: Research published in August uses data collected from ancient coral, and provides that 1,000-year glimpse Callahan mentions. (He wasn’t involved with the study.) The scientists found an uptick in El Niño amplitude that neatly mirrors when humans started pumping greenhouse gases into the atmosphere, though they didn’t attempt to attribute the shift to climate change.
paras.zh: 8 月发表的研究使用了从古代珊瑚收集的数据，并提供了卡拉汉提到的 1000 年一瞥。 （他没有参与这项研究。）科学家们发现厄尔尼诺现象的幅度有所上升，这恰好反映了人类开始向大气中排放温室气体的时间，尽管他们并没有试图将这种变化归因于气候变化。

paras.en: This year’s El Niño will provide another data point to help researchers suss things out.
paras.zh: 今年的厄尔尼诺现象将提供另一个数据点来帮助研究人员弄清楚问题。

paras.en: How Is El Niño Impacting Climate Change?
paras.zh: 厄尔尼诺现象如何影响气候变化？

paras.en: But as Callahan notes, there’s also an important question about how El Niño is layering on top of climate change.
paras.zh: 但正如卡拉汉指出的那样，还有一个重要问题是厄尔尼诺现象如何影响气候变化。

paras.en: “Even if climate change has not made the event itself stronger, even if the [sea surface temperature] anomalies are totally natural, the presence of those SSTs in a climate that has been changed by global warming might produce unprecedented impacts,” he says.
paras.zh: “即使气候变化没有使事件本身变得更加严重，即使[海面温度]异常是完全自然的，这些海表温度在因全球变暖而改变的气候中的存在可能会产生前所未有的影响，”他说。

paras.en: El Niño’s impacts on weather—known as teleconnections—are well known, from increasing the odds of drought in the Amazon and Indonesia to juicing precipitation in the Southwest US and lowering the odds of Atlantic hurricanes.
paras.zh: 厄尔尼诺现象对天气的影响（称为遥相关）是众所周知的，从增加亚马逊和印度尼西亚的干旱几率到增加美国西南部的降水并降低大西洋飓风的几率。

paras.en: Such an extreme event layered on top of climate change doesn’t mean teleconnections get thrown out the window, though. In fact, some of them may be even more intense.
paras.zh: 不过，气候变化之外的这种极端事件并不意味着远程连接会被抛到九霄云外。事实上，其中一些可能更为激烈。

paras.en: “We can no longer place as much confidence in the knowledge we’ve gathered from data regarding how El Niño manifests in terms of weather and climate in different parts of the planet,” says Estrada.
paras.zh: 埃斯特拉达说：“我们不能再对从厄尔尼诺现象在地球不同地区的天气和气候方面表现的数据中收集到的知识抱有太大信心。”

paras.en: From a risk perspective, Estrada believes it’s important to understand how the two phenomena interact and how that combination will affect societies.
paras.zh: 从风险的角度来看，埃斯特拉达认为了解这两种现象如何相互作用以及这种结合将如何影响社会非常重要。

paras.en: He and Callahan’s main concern is not merely whether this El Niño will be the most intense on record but rather the combination of an exceptional event with a climate that has warmed significantly.
paras.zh: 他和卡拉汉主要担心的不仅仅是这次厄尔尼诺现象是否会是有记录以来最强烈的一次，而是一次特殊事件与显着变暖的气候相结合。

paras.en: “Surprises are the last thing you want when you’re trying to manage risk,” Estrada says.
paras.zh: “当你试图管理风险时，意外是你最不想要的，”埃斯特拉达说。

paras.en: Callahan’s work shows that the impacts of El Niño on society are extreme, with the most severe events knocking off trillions of dollars from the global GDP. Ecosystems also suffer greatly, particularly coral reefs, which are facing a mass bleaching event.
paras.zh: 卡拉汉的研究表明，厄尔尼诺现象对社会的影响是极端的，最严重的事件使全球 GDP 损失了数万亿美元。生态系统也受到很大影响，特别是珊瑚礁，正面临大规模白化事件。

paras.en: Given this scenario, the United Nations and other international organizations have called for urgent adaptation measures to safeguard the well-being of the at-risk populations and ecosystems. Some places are already doing that: California preemptively declared a state of emergency last month.
paras.zh: 鉴于这种情况，联合国和其他国际组织呼吁采取紧急适应措施，以保障面临风险的人口和生态系统的福祉。有些地方已经在这样做了：加州上个月先发制人地宣布进入紧急状态。

paras.en: “El Niño conditions will pour fuel on the fire of a warming world. Impacts will hit even harder, travel even farther, and cross borders with devastating speed,” UN Secretary-General António Guterres said last month.
paras.zh: 联合国秘书长安东尼奥·古特雷斯上个月表示：“厄尔尼诺现象将为全球变暖火上浇油。影响将更加严重、传播更远，并以毁灭性的速度跨越边界。”

articles.title: These Midterm Races Will Decide Data Centers’ Political Fate
articles.author: Molly Taft

paras.en: Welcome back to Power Play! Each week, senior writer Molly Taft tackles a topic around this midterm season’s biggest issue: data centers. If you’ve got a question or thought for the column, feel free to shoot Molly an email at [email protected] or reach them securely on Signal at mollytaft.76.
paras.zh: 欢迎回到 Power Play！每周，资深作家莫莉·塔夫脱都会围绕本期中最大的问题讨论一个话题：数据中心。如果您对本专栏有疑问或想法，请随时通过 [email protected] 向 Molly 发送电子邮件，或通过 Signal 安全地联系他们：mollytaft.76。

paras.en: From surveillance and DOGE to Big Tech money and religious extremism, the midterms have never been more WIRED. Data centers are no exception: The public has rapidly turned on them since the beginning of the year.
paras.zh: 从监视和 DOGE 到大型科技公司的资金和宗教极端主义，中期选举从未像现在这样如此紧张。数据中心也不例外：自今年年初以来，公众迅速对它们产生了兴趣。

paras.en: The opposition is bipartisan, with many Republicans making a rare break from President Donald Trump. Candidates on both sides of the aisle are trying to attack their opponents for being pro–data center (or not anti–data center enough). I’ve spotted at least five candidates who have been given the derogatory “Data Center [Name]” moniker by their opponents, in an attempt to highlight their connections to the industry. (That includes two guys named Derek/Derrick getting this treatment.)
paras.zh: 反对派是两党的，许多共和党人罕见地与唐纳德·特朗普总统决裂。两党候选人都试图攻击对手支持数据中心（或者不够反对数据中心）。我发现至少有五名候选人被对手赋予了贬义性的“数据中心[名称]”绰号，以突显他们与该行业的联系。 （其中包括两个名叫德里克/德里克的人接受这种治疗。）

paras.en: While polling shows that pocketbook issues are likely to be top of voters’ minds, data centers are a potent-enough issue that they could swing tight races—and ultimately tip the balance of power in Congress. Here are some of the races WIRED is keeping an eye on as we approach November 3.
paras.zh: 虽然民意调查显示，钱包问题可能是选民最关心的问题，但数据中心是一个足够强大的问题，它们可能会左右激烈的竞选，并最终打破国会的权力平衡。以下是 11 月 3 日临近时《连线》杂志正在关注的一些比赛。

paras.en: The National Republican Senatorial Committee issued a memo in August warning that Democrat Sherrod Brown, running for Senate in Ohio, was hitting his opponent, Senator Jon Husted, so hard on data centers that it could tip the outcome of the race, calling it “a sleeper issue for the entire election cycle.” Brown has called Husted “the face of data centers in Ohio,” running ads that blame Husted for welcoming data centers to the state and driving energy bills up.
paras.zh: 全国共和党参议员委员会在 8 月份发布了一份备忘录，警告称，竞选俄亥俄州参议员的民主党人谢罗德·布朗 (Sherrod Brown) 在数据中心方面对对手参议员乔恩·赫斯特德 (Jon Husted) 的打击如此之大，以至于可能会影响竞选结果，并称其为“整个选举周期的潜在问题”。布朗称赫斯特德为“俄亥俄州数据中心的代表”，并投放广告指责赫斯特德欢迎数据中心来到该州并导致能源费用上涨。

paras.en: Senate Democrats have taken up Brown’s cause, torpedoing a bill sponsored by Husted and modeled after the White House’s ratepayer protection pledge, with Minority Leader Chuck Schumer calling the bill “toothless.”
paras.zh: 参议院民主党人支持布朗的事业，破坏了一项由赫斯特德发起、仿照白宫纳税人保护承诺的法案，少数党领袖查克·舒默称该法案“毫无牙齿”。

paras.en: Data centers have also seeped into many other toss-up Senate races, including in Michigan, Iowa, and Texas. But the Ohio race is still the top one to watch here.
paras.zh: 数据中心还渗透到了许多其他激烈的参议院竞选中，包括密歇根州、爱荷华州和德克萨斯州。但俄亥俄州的比赛仍然是这里最值得关注的一场比赛。

paras.en: All 435 seats in the House are up for grabs, and data centers have become flash points in dozens of races across the country. Among races labeled toss-ups by the Cook Political Report, I found numerous examples of candidates running data-center-related ads:
paras.zh: 众议院全部 435 个席位都处于争夺之中，数据中心已成为全国数十场竞选的热点。在库克政治报告标记为“难以预测”的竞选中，我发现了许多候选人投放与数据中心相关的广告的例子：

paras.en: - In Michigan’s 7th district, Will Lawrence used local opposition to data centers to help win a tough Democratic primary. Lawrence is now facing off against Republican Tom Barrett and has aired several data-center-related ads, both attacking Barrett and advertising Lawrence’s promise to “stand up to corporate power.”
paras.zh: - 在密歇根州第七选区，威尔·劳伦斯 (Will Lawrence) 利用当地对数据中心的反对，帮助赢得了一场艰难的民主党初选。劳伦斯现在正与共和党人汤姆·巴雷特对峙，并播放了几则与数据中心相关的广告，既攻击巴雷特，又宣传劳伦斯“勇敢地面对企业权力”的承诺。

paras.en: - In Pennsylvania’s 8th district, Republican incumbent Rob Bresnahan has run ads promising to be tough on the industry—despite holding data-center-related stocks and a previously friendly stance. His Democratic challenger, Paige Cognetti, has also run ads attacking the industry.
paras.zh: - 在宾夕法尼亚州第 8 选区，共和党现任议员罗布·布雷斯纳汉 (Rob Bresnahan) 投放广告，承诺对该行业采取强硬态度，尽管他持有数据中心相关股票，并且此前立场友好。他的民主党挑战者佩奇·科涅蒂(Paige Cognetti)也投放了攻击该行业的广告。

paras.en: - In Ohio’s 9th, Democratic incumbent Marcy Kaptur has run ads railing against what she says is incumbent Derek Merrin’s history of giving tax breaks to data centers. (The ads call him “Data Center Derek.”) Merrin claims that Kaptur is misrepresenting his vote on a broader bill.
paras.zh: - 在俄亥俄州第 9 届选举中，民主党现任议员马西·卡普图尔 (Marcy Kaptur) 刊登广告，抨击她所说的现任议员德里克·梅林 (Derek Merrin) 为数据中心提供税收减免的历史。 （广告称他为“数据中心德里克”。）梅林声称卡普图歪曲了他对更广泛法案的投票。

paras.en: - In Wisconsin’s 3rd district, Democrat Rebecca Cooke has aired attack ads against incumbent Derrick van Orden’s history of taking contributions from data center developers, dubbing him “DC Derrick.” (Sound familiar?) Van Orden has also shot back by highlighting Cooke’s ties to the tech industry, claiming she is “responsible for covering up pristine Wisconsin farmland” with data centers.
paras.zh: - 在威斯康星州第三选区，民主党人丽贝卡·库克（Rebecca Cooke）播放了攻击广告，攻击现任议员德里克·范·奥登（Derrick van Orden）接受数据中心开发商捐款的历史，称他为“DC Derrick”。 （听起来很熟悉？）范奥登也进行了反击，强调了库克与科技行业的联系，声称她“负责用数据中心覆盖威斯康星州的原始农田”。

paras.en: - In New York’s 17th district, incumbent Republican Mike Lawler has aired an ad slamming Democratic opponent Cait Conley’s past statements that the Hudson Valley “needs” data centers.
paras.zh: - 在纽约第 17 选区，现任共和党人迈克·劳勒 (Mike Lawler) 播放了一则广告，抨击民主党对手凯特·康利 (Cait Conley) 过去关于哈德逊河谷“需要”数据中心的言论。

paras.en: At least 20 candidates in the 36 gubernatorial races have promised to enact some kind of data center moratorium if elected, according to research from Multistate. The only true hyperscale moratorium in place in the US right now was signed in July by New York governor Kathy Hochul, who holds a comfortable lead ahead of challenger Bruce Blakeman (who supports data center development).
paras.zh: 根据 Multistate 的研究，36 名州长竞选中至少有 20 名候选人承诺，如果当选，将颁布某种形式的数据中心暂停令。美国目前唯一真正的超大规模暂停令是由纽约州州长 Kathy Hochul 在 7 月签署的，他遥遥领先于挑战者 Bruce Blakeman（支持数据中心开发）。

paras.en: Candidates without much daylight between them have still tried to gain the upper hand on the issue. In Wisconsin’s tight gubernatorial race, Republican Tom Tiffany has attacked Democrat David Crowley with ads calling him “Data Center David.” Both candidates say they support restrictions on the industry.
paras.zh: 彼此之间没有太多阳光的候选人仍然试图在这个问题上占据上风。在威斯康星州紧张的州长竞选中，共和党人汤姆·蒂芙尼（Tom Tiffany）通过广告攻击民主党人大卫·克劳利（David Crowley），称他为“数据中心大卫”。两位候选人都表示他们支持对该行业的限制。

paras.en: In states that have been hotbeds for data center activity, some candidates in tight races have been forced to pivot on the issue. Nowhere is this clearer than in Texas, where incumbent governor Greg Abbott has gone from welcoming data center development to putting a de facto moratorium on permits in less than a year. His opponent, Gina Hinojosa, says Abbott hasn’t gone far enough to regulate the industry.
paras.zh: 在一直是数据中心活动温床的州，一些竞争激烈的候选人被迫在这个问题上转向。这一点在德克萨斯州最为明显，该州现任州长格雷格·阿博特在不到一年的时间里就从欢迎数据中心开发转变为事实上暂停发放许可证。他的对手吉娜·伊诺霍萨 (Gina Hinojosa) 表示，雅培在监管该行业方面做得还不够。

paras.en: Voters in eight states are looking at more than 30 local ballot measures around data centers. Once again, Ohio is a standout here: It’s responsible for more than half of those measures, from local moratoriums to referendums around rezoning.
paras.zh: 八个州的选民正在关注围绕数据中心的 30 多项当地投票措施。俄亥俄州再次脱颖而出：其中一半以上的措施都是由俄亥俄州实施的，从当地的暂停令到围绕重新分区的公投。

paras.en: WIRED science editor Brian Kahn and I got exclusive access to a startup that wants to pull water from the air using excess heat from data centers. While atmospheric water-harvesting technology has been around for a while, the startup has a unique spin. Atoco uses materials known as metal organic frameworks, or MOFs, which won one of its founders the Nobel Prize last year. The company’s previous prototypes have all needed to be hooked up to the grid to generate enough heat to extract water from the MOFs. The new version, though, only needs waste heat from industrial facilities—like data centers—to produce water, even in arid areas.
paras.zh: 《连线》科学编辑布莱恩·卡恩（Brian Kahn）和我独家采访了一家初创公司，该公司希望利用数据中心的余热从空气中提取水。虽然大气集水技术已经存在一段时间了，但这家初创公司却有其独特之处。 Atoco 使用被称为金属有机框架（MOF）的材料，该材料的创始人之一去年获得了诺贝尔奖。该公司之前的原型都需要连接到电网，以产生足够的热量从 MOF 中提取水。不过，新版本只需要数据中心等工业设施的废热来生产水，即使在干旱地区也是如此。

paras.en: - In Memphis, Tennessee, home of Elon Musk’s SpaceX data centers, the city council postponed a vote on a data center moratorium. Business Insider has more on the “chaotic” meeting.
paras.zh: - 在埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) SpaceX 数据中心所在地田纳西州孟菲斯，市议会推迟了关于暂停数据中心的投票。 《商业内幕》对这次“混乱”的会议有更多报道。

paras.en: - Bloomberg reports that Oracle used trucks to ship in natural gas to a data center outside Salt Lake City to keep it online for more than a year—and is considering a similar move in New Mexico, where pipeline delays have held up a big project.
paras.zh: - 彭博社报道称，甲骨文使用卡车将天然气运送到盐湖城郊外的一个数据中心，使其保持在线一年多，并且正在考虑在新墨西哥州采取类似的举措，该州的管道延误导致了一个大型项目的进展。

paras.en: - As the midterms approach, environmental groups are flooding the zone with ads about the rush to build AI infrastructure powered by fossil fuels—just as Congress prepares to debate permitting reform. Heatmap has more.
paras.zh: - 随着中期选举的临近，环保组织在该地区铺满了有关急于建设由化石燃料驱动的人工智能基础设施的广告——就在国会准备辩论是否允许改革之际。热图还有更多。

articles.title: Catherine Zeta-Jones: 'Kill Jackie' heroine is 'polar opposite' of Morticia

paras.en: NEW YORK, Oct. 12 (UPI) -- Oscar-winning actress Catherine Zeta-Jones says she wanted to play the titular art dealer and assassin-target in Kill Jackie because she is completely different from Morticia Addams, the matriarch she portrays on Wednesday.
paras.zh: 纽约，10 月 12 日（UPI）——奥斯卡获奖女演员凯瑟琳·泽塔-琼斯表示，她想在《杀死杰基》中扮演名义上的艺术品商人和刺客目标，因为她与周三扮演的女族长莫蒂西亚·亚当斯完全不同。

paras.en: "To come off working with Tim Burton on Wednesday where I played such an iconic character as Morticia Addams and put my little stamp on this connotation of Wednesday and the family at large was amazing," Zeta-Jones, 57, told UPI at a New York Comic Con press conference this weekend.
paras.zh: 57 岁的泽塔-琼斯在本周末的纽约动漫展新闻发布会上告诉合众国际社：“周三结束与蒂姆·伯顿的合作，我扮演了莫蒂西亚·亚当斯这样的标志性角色，并在周三的这一内涵上留下了我的小印记，整个家庭真是太棒了。”

paras.en: When Kill Jackie series co-creator Peter Lawson gave her a copy of Aidan Truhen's book, Price You Pay, which was written for a male protagonist named Jack, the actress was immediately intrigued.
paras.zh: 当《杀死杰姬》系列联合创作者彼得·劳森送给她一本艾丹·特鲁恩的书《你要​​付出的代价》时，这位女演员立即产生了兴趣，这本书是为一位名叫杰克的男主人公写的。

paras.en: "Morticia Addams is a little bit more held together and a little bit more clipped," Zeta-Jones said.
paras.zh: “莫蒂西亚·亚当斯更加团结，也更加简洁，”泽塔-琼斯说。

paras.en: "Thinking about the gender switch to Jackie, it's the polar opposite of what I've been doing for the last two years. So, I just relished it," she recalled.
paras.zh: “考虑到杰基的性别转变，这与我过去两年所做的截然相反。所以，我只是喜欢它，”她回忆道。

paras.en: "But it was living in that dangerous, high-octane, action roller-coaster of a ride that a guy got to do so well in the book. Now I had a chance to do it on film in the series of Kill Jackie."
paras.zh: “但在书中，一个人能做得这么好，是因为生活在那种危险、高辛烷值、动作过山车的旅程中。现在我有机会在《杀死杰基》系列的电影中做到这一点。”

paras.en: With a resume that includes The Mask of Zorro, Entrapment, Chicago and Red 2, Zeta-Jones is no stranger to physically demanding roles.
paras.zh: 泽塔琼斯的履历包括《佐罗的面具》、《诱捕》、《芝加哥》和《红色2》，泽塔琼斯对体力要求较高的角色并不陌生。

paras.en: She credited her years of dance training for allowing her to move gracefully regardless of what the scene calls for.
paras.zh: 她称赞多年的舞蹈训练让她无论场景需要什么都能优雅地移动。

paras.en: "It's like doing love scenes. It's choreography," she said.
paras.zh: “这就像演爱情戏。这是编舞，”她说。

paras.en: "So, when it looks like the guy, before I spit his ear out, is throwing me around like a rag doll, I was holding on tight and I was just acting being thrown. So, if it wasn't for my dance training, I probably wouldn't know how to go about that. I would be terrified that I'd be hurt."
paras.zh: “所以，当那个家伙在我把他的耳朵吐出来之前，像布娃娃一样把我扔来扔去时，我紧紧地抓着，我只是假装被扔了。所以，如果不是因为我的舞蹈训练，我可能不知道该怎么做。我会害怕我会受伤。”

paras.en: She also jokingly noted that she has her limits and doesn't insist on doing death-defying Tom Cruise/Mission Impossible-style stunts herself.
paras.zh: 她还开玩笑地指出，她有自己的局限性，并不坚持自己做汤姆·克鲁斯/碟中谍风格的玩命特技。

paras.en: "I've got to give kudos to Tom Cruise," she said of her former Rock of Ages co-star.
paras.zh: “我必须向汤姆·克鲁斯致敬，”她谈到她的前《摇滚世纪》联合主演时说道。

paras.en: "I think he may be a crazy person because, as an actor, I see what he does, and it blows my mind," she added.
paras.zh: “我认为他可能是一个疯狂的人，因为作为一名演员，我看到他所做的事情，这让我大吃一惊，”她补充道。

paras.en: "So Mr. Writer and Mr. Producer," she addressed Tom Butterworth and Lawson, "no Tom Cruise, jumping off buildings... because then I wouldn't be able to do it."
paras.zh: “所以编剧先生和制片人先生，”她对汤姆·巴特沃斯和劳森说道，“不要让汤姆·克鲁斯跳楼……因为那样我就做不到了。”

paras.en: New episodes of Kill Jackie air on AMC+ Fridays.
paras.zh: 《杀死杰基》的新剧集在 AMC+ 周五播出。

articles.title: North Korea fires missiles after Seoul’s hypersonic weapon test

paras.en: SEOUL, Oct. 12 (UPI) -- North Korea launched several ballistic missiles toward the sea separating Korea and Japan on Monday in an apparent response to South Korea's recent hypersonic weapon test, Seoul's military said.
paras.zh: 首尔10月12日电首尔军方表示，朝鲜周一向韩日海域发射了数枚弹道导弹，这显然是对韩国最近进行的高超音速武器试验的回应。

paras.en: "At approximately 9:20 a.m. on Oct. 12, our military detected several ballistic missiles launched from the Pyongyang area of North Korea toward the East Sea," the Joint Chiefs of Staff said in a text message to reporters.
paras.zh: 参谋长联席会议在给记者的短信中说：“10月12日上午9时20分左右，我军检测到多枚从朝鲜平壤地区向东海发射的弹道导弹。”

paras.en: Some of the missiles flew more than 559 miles, the JCS said, with South Korean and U.S. authorities analyzing their specifications.
paras.zh: 参谋长联席会议表示，其中一些导弹的飞行距离超过 559 英里，韩国和美国当局正在分析其规格。

paras.en: "We assess this as a show of force in response to our successful hypersonic missile test launch on Oct. 8," JCS spokesman Jang Do-young told a press briefing Monday.
paras.zh: 联合参谋长联席会议发言人张道永 (Jang Do-young) 在周一的新闻发布会上表示：“我们认为这是对我们 10 月 8 日成功进行高超音速导弹试射的一次武力展示。”

paras.en: South Korea conducted the first test launch of its domestically developed hypersonic glide vehicle Thursday, with President Lee Jae Myung observing.
paras.zh: 周四，韩国在总统李在明的见证下，首次试射了国产高超音速滑翔飞行器。

paras.en: The vehicle successfully separated from its booster and completed its planned flight path at hypersonic speeds, the presidential office said.
paras.zh: 青瓦台表示，飞行器成功与助推器分离，并以高超音速完成了预定的飞行路线。

paras.en: Hypersonic glide vehicles travel at least five times the speed of sound and maneuver during flight, making their trajectories harder to predict and the weapons more difficult to intercept than conventional ballistic missiles.
paras.zh: 高超音速滑翔飞行器在飞行过程中的飞行速度和机动性至少是音速的五倍，这使得它们的轨迹比传统弹道导弹更难预测，武器也更难拦截。

paras.en: The North's launches are also seen as "a move to demonstrate tangible results from their five-year defense development plan and to intentionally showcase their missile capabilities," Jang said.
paras.zh: 张说，朝鲜的发射也被视为“展示其五年国防发展计划的切实成果并有意展示其导弹能力的举措”。

paras.en: Asked whether the weapons fired Monday were hypersonic or intermediate-range missiles, he said further analysis was needed.
paras.zh: 当被问及周一发射的武器是高超音速导弹还是中程导弹时，他表示需要进一步分析。

paras.en: The launches followed weeks of heightened tensions over Sept. 21 land mine explosions in the Demilitarized Zone that injured three South Korean soldiers, two seriously.
paras.zh: 9月21日，非军事区发生地雷爆炸，造成三名韩国士兵受伤，其中两人伤势严重，导致紧张局势持续数周加剧。

paras.en: South Korea's military said a joint investigation with the U.N. Command determined that North Korean troops had planted the mines south of the Military Demarcation Line, violating the Korean War armistice.
paras.zh: 韩国军方表示，与联合国军司令部的联合调查确定，朝鲜军队在军事分界线以南埋设了地雷，违反了朝鲜战争停战协定。

paras.en: Pyongyang denied responsibility and accused Seoul of fabricating its findings.
paras.zh: 平壤否认对此负责，并指责首尔捏造其调查结果。

paras.en: Jang reiterated Monday that the military considered the mine incident a clear armistice violation and a provocation, while saying authorities were still analyzing the North's intent.
paras.zh: 张周一重申，军方认为此次地雷事件明显违反停战协议和挑衅，同时表示当局仍在分析朝鲜的意图。

paras.en: North Korea last launched a ballistic missile on Oct. 3 from the Wonsan area. The state-run Korean Central News Agency reported the following day that leader Kim Jong Un oversaw the launch of an intermediate-range strategic missile to train troops operating its "hypersonic strategic weapon system."
paras.zh: 朝鲜最后一次发射弹道导弹是在 10 月 3 日，从元山地区发射。国营朝鲜中央通讯社第二天报道称，领导人金正恩监督发射了一枚中程战略导弹，以训练部队操作其“高超音速战略武器系统”。

articles.title: U.S. arrests Colombian with Maduro ties on money laundering charges

paras.en: Oct. 12 (UPI) -- Federal prosecutors on Sunday announced the arrested of a Colombian national with ties to jailed former Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro on accusations of participating in multibillion-dollar bribery and money laundering schemes.
paras.zh: 10 月 12 日（UPI）——联邦检察官周日宣布逮捕一名与被监禁的委内瑞拉前总统尼古拉斯·马杜罗有联系的哥伦比亚国民，他被指控参与数十亿美元的贿赂和洗钱计划。

paras.en: Alvaro Pulido Vargas, 62, faces two separate federal indictments, filed in 2021 and 2019, accusing him of participating in schemes to launder proceeds from bribery and fraud schemes involving nearly $2 billion in Venezuelan government contracts.
paras.zh: 62 岁的阿尔瓦罗·普利多·巴尔加斯 (Alvaro Pulido Vargas) 面临分别于 2021 年和 2019 年提起的两份联邦起诉书，指控他参与洗钱计划和欺诈计划，涉及委内瑞拉政府合同的近 20 亿美元。

paras.en: Specifics of his Sunday arrest were not immediately made public. He is expected to make his initial court appearance Tuesday in the Southern District of Florida.
paras.zh: 他周日被捕的具体细节并未立即公开。预计他将于周二在佛罗里达州南区首次出庭。

paras.en: "Alvaro Pulido Vargas is no longer a fugitive from justice," Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva of the Justice Department's Criminal Division said in a statement.
paras.zh: “阿尔瓦罗·普利多·巴尔加斯不再是逃犯，”司法部刑事司助理总检察长 A·泰森·杜瓦在一份声明中表示。

paras.en: "The message to anyone who brings their foreign bribery or money laundering schemes inside our borders: the U.S. Justice Department will pursue these schemes and prosecute those who perpetrate them."
paras.zh: “向任何将海外贿赂或洗钱计划带入我国境内的人传达的信息是：美国司法部将追查这些计划并起诉实施这些计划的人。”

paras.en: Pulido Vargas and Alex Saab, a Colombian businessman and former Venezuelan minister with close ties to Maduro, were originally charged in July 2019 on charges of laundering some $350 million connected to a bribery scheme.
paras.zh: 普利多·巴尔加斯 (Pulido Vargas) 和与马杜罗关系密切的哥伦比亚商人、委内瑞拉前部长亚历克斯·萨博 (Alex Saab) 最初于 2019 年 7 月被指控涉嫌洗钱约 3.5 亿美元，与贿赂计划有关。

paras.en: Prosecutors alleged the pair obtained a contract with the Venezuelan government to construct low-income housing units, but, instead, exploited the Caribbean nation's government-controlled exchange rate system by submitting false and fraudulent import documents for goods that were never imported and bribing officials to approve them.
paras.zh: 检察官指控两人与委内瑞拉政府签订了建造低收入住房的合同，但却利用这个加勒比国家政府控制的汇率制度，为从未进口过的货物提交虚假和欺诈性的进口文件，并贿赂官员以获得批准。

paras.en: The money was allegedly laundered via bank accounts in the Southern District of Florida and transferred to overseas accounts they controlled in an effort to conceal the scheme, federal prosecutors said.
paras.zh: 联邦检察官表示，这些资金据称是通过佛罗里达州南区的银行账户进行洗钱，并转移到他们控制的海外账户，以掩盖该计划。

paras.en: The 2021 indictment involved the alleged exploitation of Comité Local de Abastecimiento y Producción, also known as CLAP, a Venezuelan government-controlled program for the importation and distribution of food and medicine to the country's poor.
paras.zh: 2021 年的起诉书涉及涉嫌剥削当地食品和生产委员会（也称为 CLAP），这是委内瑞拉政府控制的一项计划，旨在向该国穷人进口和分发食品和药品。

paras.en: Federal prosecutors allege that the scheme ran from July 2015 to at least 2020, during which Pulido Vargas and his co-conspirators allegedly received some $1.6 billion from the Venezuelan government and laundered proceeds through bank accounts in Antigua, the United States, the United Arab Emirates and elsewhere.
paras.zh: 联邦检察官称，该计划从 2015 年 7 月持续到至少 2020 年，在此期间，普利多·巴尔加斯 (Pulido Vargas) 及其同谋从委内瑞拉政府收到约 16 亿美元，并通过安提瓜岛、美国、阿拉伯联合酋长国和其他地方的银行账户洗钱。

paras.en: The Justice Department alleges that Pulido Vargas and his co-conspirators gained the CLAP contracts by paying bribes to Venezuelan officials.
paras.zh: 司法部指控普利多·巴尔加斯 (Pulido Vargas) 及其同谋通过向委内瑞拉官员行贿获得 CLAP 合同。

paras.en: "Alvaro Pulido Vargas is accused of moving vast amounts of illicit money through a corrupt network that exploited the Venezuelan people and abused the U.S. financial system," Drug Enforcement Administration Administrator Terrance Cole said in a statement.
paras.zh: 缉毒局局长特伦斯·科尔在一份声明中表示：“阿尔瓦罗·普利多·巴尔加斯被指控通过腐败网络转移大量非法资金，剥削委内瑞拉人民并滥用美国金融体系。”

paras.en: Maduro and his wife, Cilia Flores, pleaded not guilty to narco-terrorism charges in a Manhattan federal courtroom in early January, days after the U.S. military captured them in Venezuela in a clandestine operation.
paras.zh: 一月初，马杜罗和他的妻子西莉亚·弗洛雷斯在曼哈顿联邦法庭对毒品恐怖主义指控表示不认罪，几天前，美国军方在委内瑞拉秘密行动中抓获了他们。

paras.en: Saab, described as Maduro's chief financial intermediary, pleaded guilty last month to conspiracy to launder monetary instruments, after pleading not guilty in July.
paras.zh: 萨博被描述为马杜罗的首席金融中介，在 7 月份不认罪后，上个月承认了共谋洗钱货币工具的罪名。

paras.en: Pulido Vargas had been a long-sought fugitive of the United States, which had offered of up to $10 million reward for information leading to his arrest or conviction. He was also under British sanctions.
paras.zh: 普利多·巴尔加斯 (Pulido Vargas) 是美国长期通缉的逃犯，美国悬赏高达 1000 万美元，悬赏提供导致他被捕或定罪的信息。他还受到英国的制裁。

paras.en: "His alleged actions show a blatant disregard to the Venezuelan people by corrupting government programs intended to provide critical food, medicine and housing for personal enrichment and exploiting the American financial system to do it. No amount of time or distance will stop @ThejusticeDept from working with our federal law enforcement and international partners to pursue these criminals and bring them to justice in an American courtroom," Attorney General Todd Blanche said online.
paras.zh: 司法部长托德·布兰奇在网上表示：“他被指控的行为表明了对委内瑞拉人民的公然漠视，他破坏了旨在为个人致富提供关键食品、药品和住房的政府计划，并利用美国金融体系来做到这一点。无论时间或距离如何，都无法阻止@ThejusticeDept与我们的联邦执法部门和国际合作伙伴合作，追捕这些罪犯，并在美国法庭将他们绳之以法。”

articles.title: Harry Styles Dedicates Moment to Oscar Belgal After ICE Shooting: ‘Look After Each Other,’ He Tells NYC Crowd
articles.author: Ashley Iasimone

paras.en: On Saturday night, Harry Styles asked a sold-out Madison Square Garden crowd to turn their attention to Oscar Belgal, the 28-year-old man who was shot by ICE in his car in the Bronx, New York City, earlier this week while his 5-year-old son was in the backseat.
paras.zh: 周六晚上，哈里·斯泰尔斯 (Harry Styles) 要求麦迪逊广场花园的观众将注意力转向奥斯卡·贝尔加尔 (Oscar Belgal)，这名 28 岁的男子本周早些时候在纽约市布朗克斯区的汽车中被 ICE 枪击，当时他 5 岁的儿子坐在后座上。

paras.en: “I just want us to take a moment to think about Oscar Belgal tonight,” said Styles, guitar in hand before performing “Sign of the Times,” one of the final songs on his Together, Together setlist on Saturday (Oct. 10). Concertgoers captured the moment and uploaded the clip to TikTok, as they’ve done with many of Styles’ interactions with fans throughout the star’s 30-night residency at the Garden.
paras.zh: “我只是想让我们今晚花点时间想想奥斯卡·贝尔格尔，”斯泰尔斯在周六（10 月 10 日）演唱《Together, Together》歌单中的最后一首歌曲《Sign of the Times》之前手握吉他说道。音乐会观众捕捉到了这一时刻，并将这段视频上传到 TikTok，就像他们在这位明星在花园举行的 30 晚驻场期间与歌迷的许多互动一样。

paras.en: “I want us to just think, [to] remember, to just look after each other,” Styles told the audience in a speech in which he didn’t say “ICE,” but seemingly referenced the situation with ICE — and the administration’s deportation agenda — after saying Belgal’s name.
paras.zh: “我希望我们只是思考、记住、互相照顾，”斯泰尔斯在一次演讲中告诉观众，他在演讲中没有说“ICE”，但在说出贝尔加尔的名字后，似乎提到了 ICE 的情况以及政府的驱逐议程。

paras.en: “It is up to us to make the cities that we live in places we want to see,” Styles said. “It’s up to us to make the world a place that we want to see, that we want to give to our children. So please continue looking after each other, and remember, your friends, the people you love, the people who don’t look like you and aren’t born where you are from: they deserve respect, love, dignity.”
paras.zh: “我们有责任把我们居住的城市建设成我们想要看到的地方，”斯泰尔斯说。 “我们有责任让这个世界成为我们想要看到的、我们想要给我们的孩子的地方。所以请继续互相照顾，并记住，你的朋友、你爱的人、那些长得不像你、出生地不是你的人：他们应该得到尊重、爱和尊严。”

paras.en: “Please get home safely and look after each other,” Styles urged the crowd.
paras.zh: “请安全回家并互相照顾，”斯泰尔斯敦促人群。

paras.en: On Thursday, Belgal was backing his car into a parking spot in the Marble Hill neighborhood with his young son in tow when he was surrounded by Immigration and Customs Enforcement officers in plain clothes. His vehicle started to move forward, and he was shot in the neck, according to NYPD commissioner Jessica S. Tisch, who says at least one ICE officer fired seven shots.
paras.zh: 周四，贝尔加拉着他的小儿子，将车倒进大理石山附近的一个停车位，当时他被身着便衣的移民和海关执法人员包围。纽约市警察局局长杰西卡·S·蒂什 (Jessica S. Tisch) 表示，他的车辆开始向前行驶，他的颈部中弹，至少一名 ICE 官员开了七枪。

paras.en: City police, who are not involved in federal immigration enforcement, arrived at the scene after hearing a report of shots fired and transported Belgal to the hospital. Belgal is now being held at Metropolitan Detention Center in Brooklyn, while the child is safe and in the care of a family member.
paras.zh: 不参与联邦移民执法的市警察在听到枪击报告后赶到现场，并将贝尔加尔送往医院。贝尔加尔目前被关押在布鲁克林大都会拘留中心，孩子很安全，并由家人照顾。

paras.en: Federal officials described Belgal as an “illegal alien gang member” from the Dominican Republic who refused to get out of his car and “smashed into two government vehicles.”
paras.zh: 联邦官员将贝尔加尔描述为来自多米尼加共和国的“非法外籍帮派成员”，他拒绝下车并“撞上了两辆政府车辆”。

paras.en: Tisch reported Belgal has had two prior arrests in New York City: “One for robbery in 2023, in which he pleaded guilty to fourth-degree grand larceny and received five years’ probation, and one for criminal sale of a controlled substance in 2025, which is still pending.”
paras.zh: 蒂什报道称，贝尔加尔此前曾在纽约市被捕过两次：“一次是在 2023 年因抢劫被捕，他承认了四级盗窃罪并获得了五年缓刑；另一次是在 2025 年因非法销售受管制物质而被捕，目前该案仍在审理中。”

paras.en: Mayor Zohran Mamdani held a press conference on Thursday, declaring, “What happened today was an outrage.” He stated, “There is no explanation for these tactics. There is no explanation for federal officers firing this many rounds into a car that has a 5-year-old in the car. There is no explanation.”
paras.zh: 市长佐赫兰·马姆达尼 (Zohran Mamdani) 周四举行新闻发布会，宣称“今天发生的事情令人愤慨。”他表示，“这些战术没有任何解释。联邦官员向一辆载有 5 岁儿童的汽车发射这么多子弹，没有任何解释。没有任何解释。”

paras.en: Mamdani said, “ICE agents surrounded the man’s vehicle before opening fire. They wore construction vests and masks that concealed their faces. There was no reasonable way to identify them as ICE agents. School had just gotten out. The street was crowded with families and children. When ICE agents opened fire, a 5-year-old child — a 5-year-old child — was in the backseat of the car. Thank God that child is physically unharmed.”
paras.zh: 马姆达尼说，“ICE特工在开枪前包围了该男子的车辆。他们穿着建筑背心，戴着遮住脸的面具。没有合理的方法来识别他们是ICE特工。学校刚刚放学。街上挤满了家庭和孩子。当ICE特工开枪时，一个5岁的孩子——一个5岁的孩子——坐在车的后座上。感谢上帝，这个孩子身体没有受伤。”

paras.en: “Tonight, a 5-year-old child sits traumatized and terrified,” the mayor said at the time. “Tonight, millions of our neighbors are wondering whether they will be safe on our streets, in our schools, at their work sites. Tonight, New Yorkers across the five boroughs are asking whether their civil liberties will be respected, whether law and order is supposed to look like a man carrying a long gun, wearing a mask.”
paras.zh: “今晚，一名 5 岁的孩子遭受了创伤和恐惧，”市长当时说道。 “今晚，我们数以百万计的邻居想知道他们在我们的街道、学校和工作场所是否安全。今晚，五个行政区的纽约人都在问他们的公民自由是否会得到尊重，法律和秩序是否应该看起来像一个拿着长枪、戴着面具的人。”
